title: How to Learn a Language #3: Why Studying Grammar Can Be Bad
description: Did you study grammar to learn how to speak your native language? In this video we explain why studying grammar not only is unnecessary, but that it can actually be harmful if your goal is to speak with fluidity.
subtitles:
WEBVTT
Kind: captions
Language: en

00:00:00.480 --> 00:00:03.100
But, what about the grammar?

00:00:03.120 --> 00:00:07.600
We need to understand why, the reason why certain grammar is used, right?

00:00:07.600 --> 00:00:13.620
Well no, we don't need to. And you don't need it either.

00:00:13.620 --> 00:00:16.920
And I realized this when I was learning English,

00:00:16.920 --> 00:00:21.500
and then I confirmed it when I learned Japanese and Thai.

00:00:21.500 --> 00:00:28.040
And the research confirms it. The research confirms that it is better, that the result is better

00:00:28.040 --> 00:00:34.940
when grammar is not studied, when rules are not learned, when you don't learn about the why.

00:00:34.940 --> 00:00:39.260
And note this, I am not saying that grammar

00:00:39.260 --> 00:00:44.920
is not important, because the only important thing is communication. No, no, no.

00:00:44.920 --> 00:00:50.860
I'm not saying: "fine! it's okay, it's not a problem to make mistakes. No, no.

00:00:50.860 --> 00:00:56.920
What I am saying is that with comprehensible input you will get a better result

00:00:56.920 --> 00:01:02.320
without studying the grammar. You will be able to use grammar better.

00:01:02.320 --> 00:01:08.100
That you will have better results because you will make fewer mistakes,

00:01:08.100 --> 00:01:12.420
especially fewer mistakes that accompany us forever,

00:01:12.420 --> 00:01:17.880
fewer of those mistakes that seem like we never manage to fix.

00:01:17.880 --> 00:01:22.640
And not only that, but you can also learn with less stress,

00:01:22.640 --> 00:01:28.740
in a more fun way, and also in a way that works for everyone.

00:01:28.740 --> 00:01:34.660
Studying grammar, studying the rules, some people are good at that.

00:01:34.660 --> 00:01:40.960
There are certain people who like to study grammar

00:01:40.960 --> 00:01:45.960
and are good at learning the rules and taking tests

00:01:45.960 --> 00:01:49.060
in which they are asked about grammar.

00:01:49.060 --> 00:01:53.420
But learning with Comprehensible Input

00:01:53.420 --> 00:02:02.060
works for everyone. You don't have to do be good at that kind of tasks, at learning and apply grammar rules.

00:02:02.060 --> 00:02:06.480
And sometimes in messages or comments,

00:02:06.480 --> 00:02:10.780
people tell me: "But Pablo, I need grammar."

00:02:14.720 --> 00:02:21.780
And my answer is: no. You don't know you need it. You think you need it,

00:02:21.780 --> 00:02:27.100
because when they explain the grammar, or they explain something to you about the language,

00:02:27.100 --> 00:02:34.680
you understand it and it seems that you have achieved something, right? You get the impression: "Oh! Today I know something more."

00:02:34.680 --> 00:02:38.540
But that is explicit knowledge.

00:02:38.540 --> 00:02:43.980
That cannot be converted into implicit knowledge of grammar,

00:02:43.980 --> 00:02:49.340
it cannot be converted into subconscious knowledge, which is what we use

00:02:49.340 --> 00:02:52.820
when we speak a language, when we have a conversation.

00:02:52.820 --> 00:02:57.980
The only way you would know you need that grammar

00:02:57.980 --> 00:03:02.680
is if you had done what I've done. If you had learned a language

00:03:02.680 --> 00:03:08.600
without using grammar, without learning it. If you had spent the time you need

00:03:08.600 --> 00:03:12.820
to really acquire a language and it hadn't worked,

00:03:12.820 --> 00:03:18.060
then okay, maybe you could conclude that you need grammar.

00:03:18.060 --> 00:03:21.060
But if you have never done it, you don't know.

00:03:21.060 --> 00:03:24.080
Also, look within yourself,

00:03:24.080 --> 00:03:28.240
because if you have learned a language, any language,

00:03:28.240 --> 00:03:31.560
if you have learned it to certain degree,

00:03:31.560 --> 00:03:37.040
you will have realized at some point that there is something you know

00:03:37.040 --> 00:03:41.780
that you don't know why you know it. You don't know how you learned it.

00:03:41.780 --> 00:03:44.460
You don't remember learning it.

00:03:44.460 --> 00:03:47.480
Maybe there is some grammar that you understand,

00:03:47.480 --> 00:03:53.220
or someone makes a mistake and you know that it's a mistake but you don't know exactly why.

00:03:53.260 --> 00:03:59.140
Or maybe, having a conversation you said a word or used an expression

00:03:59.140 --> 00:04:01.340
that you don't remember learning.

00:04:01.340 --> 00:04:07.300
That is because you have learned it with Comprehensible Input, not studying the rules.

00:04:07.300 --> 00:04:12.360
And this way you can prove to yourself that this works.

00:04:12.360 --> 00:04:18.140
Other people tell me: "But Pablo, I like it, I really like grammar."

00:04:18.140 --> 00:04:21.020
I know! I like it too,

00:04:21.020 --> 00:04:25.020
but liking it is not the same as it working, right?

00:04:25.020 --> 00:04:30.940
No matter how much you like it, if it doesn't work, it won't just start working suddenly.

00:04:30.940 --> 00:04:36.120
If you like it, study grammar and learn the grammar. But

00:04:36.120 --> 00:04:42.740
I recommend you do it later on. That you do it once you already have a good level in the language.

00:04:42.740 --> 00:04:46.300
Once you can communicate, you can speak in the language,

00:04:46.300 --> 00:04:50.560
then yes, study grammar if you want to learn all the rules.

00:04:50.560 --> 00:04:55.840
But if you learn grammar, if you study grammar rules

00:04:55.840 --> 00:04:59.620
before having a good level in the language,

00:04:59.620 --> 00:05:02.040
it will get in the way.

00:05:02.040 --> 00:05:06.960
When you are listening to something, listening to someone speak, you will be thinking

00:05:06.960 --> 00:05:12.600
about grammar rules, you will not be thinking about trying to understand the meaning.

00:05:12.600 --> 00:05:18.160
When you're speaking it's even worse. You'll be thinking about rules

00:05:18.160 --> 00:05:25.680
when you should be thinking about the topic you want to talk about, about what you want to say to the other person.

00:05:25.680 --> 00:05:30.100
You cannot be thinking at the same time about the topic you want to talk about

00:05:30.100 --> 00:05:34.320
and about how you are going to say it. About what words or what grammar you are going to use.

00:05:34.320 --> 00:05:40.140
So, how is grammar acquired with comprehensible input?

00:05:40.140 --> 00:05:45.660
What happens? What happens in our head to be able to acquire grammar?

00:05:45.660 --> 00:05:50.540
Well, first, when we learn a language with Comprehensible Input,

00:05:50.540 --> 00:05:55.860
before we start getting used to the grammar,

00:05:55.860 --> 00:05:58.640
we need to learn some words.

00:05:58.640 --> 00:06:03.340
First, our brain, our mind, needs some words.

00:06:03.340 --> 00:06:09.220
And once we know the meaning of some words,

00:06:09.220 --> 00:06:13.480
your mind begins to realize:

00:06:13.480 --> 00:06:17.460
"Ok, well, this word goes after this other one, not before."

00:06:17.460 --> 00:06:20.780
We begin to learn, we begin to get used

00:06:20.780 --> 00:06:24.920
to the order. To some parts of the word order.

00:06:24.920 --> 00:06:30.140
And to learn many things about grammar we need quite few words.

00:06:30.140 --> 00:06:35.220
We need to understand almost every word in a sentence.

00:06:35.220 --> 00:06:37.320
For example, for connectors.

00:06:37.320 --> 00:06:43.080
If there is a word, a short word in the middle of a sentence that connects two parts,

00:06:43.080 --> 00:06:47.560
unless we really understand the meaning of the two parts,

00:06:47.560 --> 00:06:55.260
our brain, our head, will not be able to guess, to understand how

00:06:55.260 --> 00:07:00.520
it connects the two parts. What that word that connects the two parts does.

00:07:00.520 --> 00:07:05.460
So, some things, some parts of grammar and some words

00:07:05.460 --> 00:07:09.240
are learned surprisingly late. They are learned quite late.

00:07:09.240 --> 00:07:14.600
For example "ser" and "estar." Many things like this are learned much later

00:07:14.600 --> 00:07:20.120
than they are studied in a regular language course or class.

00:07:20.120 --> 00:07:22.380
But don't worry,

00:07:22.380 --> 00:07:26.660
because what takes the most time when learning a language is vocabulary.

00:07:26.660 --> 00:07:31.880
When you know enough vocabulary, when you get to the point with your vocabulary

00:07:31.880 --> 00:07:35.460
that you can have a conversation without problems,

00:07:35.460 --> 00:07:40.640
the grammar will be there. You will know the grammar well. Don't worry about it.

00:07:40.640 --> 00:07:43.240
For me, the grammar of a language

00:07:43.240 --> 00:07:47.720
is always the least of my worries when I am learning a language.

00:07:47.720 --> 00:07:51.800
And well, I hope that with this video I have cleared up doubts

00:07:51.800 --> 00:07:55.760
and I hope to calm some concerns

00:07:55.760 --> 00:07:58.800
about the study of grammar

00:07:58.800 --> 00:08:03.420
so that you realize that it is not that we are ignoring grammar,

00:08:03.420 --> 00:08:05.940
but that we are giving you the tools

00:08:05.940 --> 00:08:09.080
to learn it well, to learn it intuitively.

00:08:09.080 --> 00:08:13.820
To learn grammar subconsciously and not consciously.

00:08:13.820 --> 00:08:15.980
Okay? Alright,

00:08:15.980 --> 00:08:18.000
see you in the next video!

title: How to Learn a Language #1: My Language Learning Journey
description: How did Pablo come to speak 6 languages fluently? What did he learn on his journey that led him to come up with the method that lies behind Dreaming Spanish?
subtitles:
WEBVTT
Kind: captions
Language: en

00:00:00.780 --> 00:00:01.840
Hi!

00:00:01.840 --> 00:00:08.380
Welcome to this series of videos on how to learn Spanish.

00:00:08.380 --> 00:00:13.060
If you are watching this, it is because you already know Dreaming Spanish,

00:00:13.060 --> 00:00:17.340
you have watched some Dreaming Spanish videos,

00:00:17.340 --> 00:00:22.560
but in these videos I want to explain why,

00:00:22.560 --> 00:00:25.720
why Dreaming Spanish works,

00:00:25.720 --> 00:00:28.860
how to take advantage of Dreaming Spanish,

00:00:28.860 --> 00:00:32.840
how to learn Spanish well with Dreaming Spanish

00:00:32.840 --> 00:00:36.980
and with other resources. What is really the best way

00:00:36.980 --> 00:00:42.920
right now to learn Spanish well, and to learn Spanish fast.

00:00:42.920 --> 00:00:45.720
So, in this first video,

00:00:45.720 --> 00:00:53.040
the first thing I want to talk about is: who am I, and why am I doing this.

00:00:53.040 --> 00:00:57.040
This way, maybe you'll understand a little better

00:00:57.040 --> 00:01:00.500
why I am using this method,

00:01:00.500 --> 00:01:03.720
why I think this method is the best one you can use.

00:01:03.720 --> 00:01:06.900
So, first I will talk a little about myself.

00:01:06.900 --> 00:01:10.480
My name is Pablo Román, I'm from Spain,

00:01:10.480 --> 00:01:14.460
and that's why I teach Spanish, that's why I make Spanish videos, right?

00:01:14.460 --> 00:01:16.860
Because my native language is Spanish.

00:01:16.860 --> 00:01:22.800
So, the first foreign language that I learned well

00:01:22.800 --> 00:01:28.860
was English. And I studied English a little in school, like everyone else,

00:01:28.860 --> 00:01:33.820
but then I continued learning by myself,

00:01:33.820 --> 00:01:40.900
and I continued learning by doing things like: watching movies and series, reading books,

00:01:40.900 --> 00:01:44.540
reading things online, reading websites.

00:01:44.540 --> 00:01:47.820
But when I went abroad to live,

00:01:47.820 --> 00:01:52.600
when I went to live in another country, and I had to use English every day

00:01:52.600 --> 00:02:00.760
I realized one thing. I realized that: Oh! I am using phrases,

00:02:00.760 --> 00:02:06.560
I'm saying phrases that use grammar that I was never taught.

00:02:06.560 --> 00:02:12.820
I was never taught to use these words in this way

00:02:12.820 --> 00:02:16.380
but I know how to use them. I know they sound natural.

00:02:16.380 --> 00:02:18.760
I know that I am not misusing it.

00:02:18.760 --> 00:02:23.680
And later, I started to learn Japanese.

00:02:23.680 --> 00:02:30.600
Totally by chance. It had nothing to do. But I started to learn Japanese.

00:02:30.600 --> 00:02:33.820
And this time I started to learn it

00:02:33.820 --> 00:02:37.360
from the beginning in this natural way.

00:02:37.360 --> 00:02:41.579
With input, right? Reading and watching series,

00:02:41.579 --> 00:02:44.980
watching movies, listening to a lot of Japanese.

00:02:44.980 --> 00:02:49.760
And I realized that this way

00:02:49.760 --> 00:02:54.860
of getting used to grammar, of getting grammar to feel natural to you,

00:02:54.860 --> 00:02:58.320
is not just for advanced levels,

00:02:58.320 --> 00:03:01.560
it can be done from the beginning.

00:03:01.560 --> 00:03:04.000
When you start learning a language

00:03:04.000 --> 00:03:08.720
you can already learn this way. In the same way that I improved in English.

00:03:08.720 --> 00:03:13.540
Which is with input only. Just by listening, reading, etc.

00:03:13.540 --> 00:03:18.360
So, I learned Japanese without using textbooks.

00:03:18.360 --> 00:03:22.740
I learned Japanese without going to class. I have never been to Japanese classes.

00:03:22.740 --> 00:03:27.400
And I learned it very well. My level of Japanese really was very good.

00:03:27.400 --> 00:03:31.480
And then I decided: "Wow! Well,

00:03:31.480 --> 00:03:37.820
if I have been able to learn Japanese very well without using textbooks, without going to class,

00:03:37.820 --> 00:03:40.440
and having fun, having a lot of fun,

00:03:40.440 --> 00:03:43.840
then I'm sure I can teach other people

00:03:43.840 --> 00:03:46.080
to learn the same way."

00:03:46.080 --> 00:03:51.040
So I decided to look for a method, a way to learn languages

00:03:51.040 --> 00:03:55.980
that works better, and that works for everyone. That everyone can use.

00:03:55.980 --> 00:04:03.800
That's when I learned about Comprehensible Input, right?

00:04:03.940 --> 00:04:09.840
I learned about it, I started reading a lot of research, reading papers and reading books,

00:04:09.840 --> 00:04:14.220
and still now I keep reading research and keep reading books

00:04:14.220 --> 00:04:17.470
to try to keep improving my method

00:04:17.470 --> 00:04:20.420
and help you learn in the most efficient way.

00:04:20.420 --> 00:04:25.300
Then I discovered a school here in Bangkok, in Thailand,

00:04:25.300 --> 00:04:31.380
that teaches Thai using only Comprehensible Input.

00:04:31.380 --> 00:04:34.860
And I decided to try it, I decided to try that method,

00:04:34.860 --> 00:04:40.680
I came here, I studied Thai for 1200 hours

00:04:40.680 --> 00:04:45.180
and here I bring you all the things that I have learned

00:04:45.180 --> 00:04:51.400
reading research, and learning Thai myself, and learning Japanese.

00:04:51.400 --> 00:04:55.540
Everything I've learned I've condensed in this method

00:04:55.540 --> 00:04:57.840
and I bring it to you with Dreaming Spanish.

00:04:57.840 --> 00:05:01.860
Because after learning this method

00:05:01.860 --> 00:05:05.700
I realized that there are simply no resources.

00:05:05.710 --> 00:05:12.540
There are no videos, no audios, that are easy enough to understand.

00:05:12.540 --> 00:05:16.160
Especially for beginners, for beginner level people,

00:05:16.160 --> 00:05:19.560
or even intermediate level, it is very difficult

00:05:19.560 --> 00:05:21.980
to find resources of this kind.

00:05:21.980 --> 00:05:27.960
That's why I decided that I had to start making videos myself, to create Dreaming Spanish.

00:05:27.960 --> 00:05:32.160
And here is where the first video ends. In the next video

00:05:32.160 --> 00:05:36.220
I will explain what is Comprehensible Input,

00:05:36.220 --> 00:05:37.920
why it is important,

00:05:37.920 --> 00:05:42.640
and how to learn Spanish with Dreaming Spanish,

00:05:42.640 --> 00:05:45.220
and with other resources.

00:05:45.220 --> 00:05:46.320
See you!

title: How to Learn a Language #6: When and How to Read
description: Reading is another way of receiving input and acquiring the language. In this video we explain when is the best moment to start reading to help you learn the language in the most efficient and enjoyable way.
subtitles:
WEBVTT
Kind: captions
Language: en

00:00:00.380 --> 00:00:01.720
Hello!

00:00:01.720 --> 00:00:04.720
In the last video I explained

00:00:04.720 --> 00:00:08.180
when and how to start talking.

00:00:08.180 --> 00:00:13.900
And now, in this video, I want to talk about reading. About how and when to start reading.

00:00:13.900 --> 00:00:18.720
Because the reading is very good. It works very well to learn a language.

00:00:18.720 --> 00:00:22.000
And I read a lot. I have read a lot to learn English,

00:00:22.000 --> 00:00:24.460
I keep reading to learn Japanese,

00:00:24.460 --> 00:00:28.260
and depending on your goal with the language

00:00:28.260 --> 00:00:31.460
reading will be an important part

00:00:31.460 --> 00:00:37.120
of your learning and it will be an important part of the time you spend learning a language.

00:00:37.120 --> 00:00:41.280
But I also do not recommend reading

00:00:41.280 --> 00:00:44.600
since the beginning. Reading when you are beginners.

00:00:44.600 --> 00:00:47.180
And in this video I will explain why.

00:00:47.180 --> 00:00:51.440
So, as I told you, reading is very good.

00:00:51.440 --> 00:00:54.980
There is only one problem. In this case there is only one problem.

00:00:54.980 --> 00:00:59.140
And the only problem of starting to read, and, should I also say, to write,

00:00:59.140 --> 00:01:03.420
to start reading and writing very early on, is  pronunciation.

00:01:03.420 --> 00:01:06.620
Really the only problem is pronunciation.

00:01:06.620 --> 00:01:14.580
So, if you are only interested in being able to read and write in the language,

00:01:14.580 --> 00:01:19.480
or you're only interested in watching movies, TV series,

00:01:19.480 --> 00:01:23.620
and you will never need to speak the language,

00:01:23.620 --> 00:01:27.460
or it’s not important for you to know how to speak the language,

00:01:27.460 --> 00:01:30.920
then it's not a problem. You can start reading

00:01:30.920 --> 00:01:36.780
anytime you want. Already from the beginning. If you can find texts that are understandable,

00:01:36.780 --> 00:01:40.600
you can find reading materials that are understandable,

00:01:40.600 --> 00:01:44.080
you can start reading since the beginning, no problem.

00:01:44.080 --> 00:01:49.840
But, if you want to have a good accent and a good pronunciation,

00:01:49.840 --> 00:01:54.380
for people to understand you without problems, to not have problems communicating,

00:01:54.380 --> 00:01:59.280
for people to understand each you without getting tired, without having to make a lot of effort

00:01:59.280 --> 00:02:01.640
to understand what you are saying,

00:02:01.640 --> 00:02:04.600
I recommend you not to read at the beginning.

00:02:04.600 --> 00:02:09.020
What is the problem with reading? Well, pronunciation, right?

00:02:09.020 --> 00:02:15.220
Because when we read, we get letters and we have to make words

00:02:15.220 --> 00:02:19.620
sound in our head.

00:02:19.620 --> 00:02:24.180
We pronounce the words in our head, they sound in our head.

00:02:24.180 --> 00:02:27.720
And what's the issue? That if we are learning a new language

00:02:27.720 --> 00:02:32.120
and we still don't know the sounds of the language well,

00:02:32.120 --> 00:02:36.000
we haven't really got used to what the language sounds like,

00:02:36.000 --> 00:02:42.140
the language is not going to sound in our head. It can't, because those sounds don't exist in our head yet.

00:02:42.140 --> 00:02:45.620
So, what are they going to sound like? How are we going to read the letters?

00:02:45.620 --> 00:02:48.260
We'll either read the letters with

00:02:48.260 --> 00:02:52.069
the sounds that our mother tongue,

00:02:52.069 --> 00:02:56.380
or with the sounds that we believe that the language has,

00:02:56.380 --> 00:03:00.100
that we have studied, perhaps we have learned,

00:03:00.100 --> 00:03:05.860
but that is not something as clear as actually having heard the language

00:03:05.860 --> 00:03:11.360
for many hours and having got used to the sound of the language.

00:03:11.360 --> 00:03:14.440
As I told you in the "Comprehensible Input" video,

00:03:14.440 --> 00:03:19.440
it's not the same to have studied, to know the rules, or in this case to know

00:03:19.440 --> 00:03:23.600
the position of our mouth and of
the tongue, it's not the same

00:03:23.600 --> 00:03:27.080
to really know, intuitively,

00:03:27.080 --> 00:03:30.540
know which sound really is right,

00:03:30.540 --> 00:03:34.320
how you go from one sound to the next sound,

00:03:34.320 --> 00:03:39.700
what is the rhythm, what is the intonation that native speakers use...

00:03:39.700 --> 00:03:44.580
All this must really be learned subconsciously.

00:03:44.580 --> 00:03:49.220
You have to listen to the language hundreds of hours and there is no way around this

00:03:49.220 --> 00:03:52.080
to really get this mental image

00:03:52.080 --> 00:03:56.040
of the sound of the language. You have to listen to it for hundreds of hours.

00:03:56.040 --> 00:04:00.720
So, I recommend starting to read when we  already know very clearly

00:04:00.720 --> 00:04:05.920
what the language sounds like, when there is no more uncertainty

00:04:05.920 --> 00:04:09.240
about which sound is which when we hear it,

00:04:09.240 --> 00:04:16.889
when the sounds of the language begin to seem familiar, they begin to seem normal.

00:04:16.889 --> 00:04:22.280
My experience when learning a language is that, at first, the sound of the language

00:04:22.280 --> 00:04:30.340
makes me feel something. It makes me feel that it's pretty, or that it's ugly, or that it's rough, or that it's soft...

00:04:30.340 --> 00:04:36.040
But when I get to learn the sound of language well, I stop feeling those things.

00:04:36.040 --> 00:04:39.780
It just seems normal, it seems regular.

00:04:39.780 --> 00:04:43.080
"Well, yeah sure, that's the way you talk, that's what it sounds like."

00:04:43.080 --> 00:04:47.280
I stop having any feelings about the sound of the language.

00:04:47.280 --> 00:04:53.700
This can be a way of knowing if you really know the sound of the language.

00:04:53.700 --> 00:04:58.300
So, same as with speaking, there is a compromise.

00:04:58.300 --> 00:05:02.280
When do you want to start reading,

00:05:02.280 --> 00:05:04.580
because there are also advantages to reading,

00:05:04.580 --> 00:05:08.280
reading can help us learn vocabulary

00:05:08.280 --> 00:05:10.840
which is only used in writing,

00:05:10.840 --> 00:05:15.139
vocabulary used in different situations.

00:05:15.140 --> 00:05:20.500
For example, you may not find many videos about recent news,

00:05:20.500 --> 00:05:23.880
or about literature, or about science fiction,

00:05:23.880 --> 00:05:27.500
and you can read books on those topics

00:05:27.500 --> 00:05:30.840
and learn vocabulary that's used in those situations, right?

00:05:30.840 --> 00:05:35.020
So, here again there is a compromise. You have to choose

00:05:35.020 --> 00:05:40.360
between getting to have a very good accent if you leave reading for later,

00:05:40.360 --> 00:05:42.900
and you have to compare that with the value

00:05:42.900 --> 00:05:48.080
of learning vocabulary for the topics that you really want to learn.

00:05:48.080 --> 00:05:52.460
and also with learning spelling, with learning

00:05:52.460 --> 00:05:58.500
how words are written. What letters are used. If it's written with a "b" or a "v",

00:05:58.500 --> 00:06:02.880
or with a "g" or a "j", if there is an "h" or not...

00:06:02.880 --> 00:06:07.320
Well, to learn spelling we need to read a lot.

00:06:07.320 --> 00:06:12.640
And to really be able to write well, without making mistakes, without making errors,

00:06:12.640 --> 00:06:18.169
we need to read a lot. So, you have to make this compromise. Consider

00:06:18.169 --> 00:06:24.120
how important having a good accent is for you compared to

00:06:24.120 --> 00:06:30.740
when do you want to start being able to write well, to learn specific vocabulary... Right?

00:06:30.740 --> 00:06:33.840
Also, you can do this in Spanish

00:06:33.840 --> 00:06:37.540
because in Spanish you have Dreaming Spanish. You have many hours

00:06:37.540 --> 00:06:40.600
of videos to listen to, of easy videos.

00:06:40.600 --> 00:06:47.020
But if you are learning another language, another language in which you don't have something like Dreaming Spanish,

00:06:47.020 --> 00:06:51.180
it can be hard to find materials, find videos

00:06:51.180 --> 00:06:54.000
which are easy to understand,

00:06:54.000 --> 00:06:57.860
and then you may have to

00:06:57.860 --> 00:07:02.620
rely much more on the written language, right?

00:07:02.620 --> 00:07:05.220
On texts, or on books.

00:07:05.220 --> 00:07:10.380
If you are learning another language, then you may not have any other option

00:07:10.380 --> 00:07:14.060
and you may have to start reading, or practice reading, early, right?

00:07:14.060 --> 00:07:19.180
And in that case, yes, I would recommend doing so because it's the most practical thing to do. The way

00:07:19.180 --> 00:07:21.180
you are going to learn faster.

00:07:21.180 --> 00:07:25.820
In any case, when you start reading

00:07:25.820 --> 00:07:31.420
I recommend you do extensive reading.

00:07:31.420 --> 00:07:35.660
And I have a video about that. You can search "extensive reading"

00:07:35.660 --> 00:07:39.180
on my YouTube channel, and there I explain it in a lot of detail.

00:07:39.180 --> 00:07:42.820
Now I'm going to explain it a little more generally.

00:07:42.820 --> 00:07:47.220
Extensive reading refers to reading for pleasure,

00:07:47.220 --> 00:07:49.340
to read things we like to read.

00:07:49.340 --> 00:07:53.680
Just as I explained in the video about how to watch Dreaming Spanish.

00:07:53.680 --> 00:07:58.320
I explained that you have to try to understand the meaning

00:07:58.320 --> 00:08:01.680
and not pay attention to the vocabulary or the grammar,

00:08:01.680 --> 00:08:03.980
Extensive reading is the same.

00:08:03.980 --> 00:08:07.889
Read something that interests you, that you find interesting,

00:08:07.889 --> 00:08:11.400
read something that is at a good level, something of which you understand

00:08:11.400 --> 00:08:15.480
ideally 98% of the words,

00:08:15.480 --> 00:08:20.600
where there is only one word in 50 that you don't understand,

00:08:20.600 --> 00:08:25.500
and that you read without using the dictionary. That you read things that are

00:08:25.500 --> 00:08:29.560
easy, so you don't need to use the dictionary.

00:08:29.560 --> 00:08:32.620
But, even for words you don't understand,

00:08:32.620 --> 00:08:37.840
don't use the dictionary. Just keep reading,

00:08:37.840 --> 00:08:41.840
since you will find that word again in other contexts,

00:08:41.840 --> 00:08:46.700
that will help you to really understand how that word is used.

00:08:46.700 --> 00:08:53.320
And when you do extensive reading I also recommend you keep a list of books you've read.

00:08:53.320 --> 00:08:56.280
I'm doing that right now for Japanese.

00:08:56.280 --> 00:08:58.820
I write down all the books I have read,

00:08:58.820 --> 00:09:01.900
and for each book I calculate, more or less,

00:09:01.900 --> 00:09:07.460
I look at how many words are on a page and calculate, according to the number of pages in the book,

00:09:07.460 --> 00:09:11.880
How many words are in the whole book. Then I write down that number

00:09:11.880 --> 00:09:16.220
and I add them up. I add up the number of words I have read.

00:09:16.220 --> 00:09:21.870
And I have a goal. I have set a goal for how many words I have to read, right?

00:09:21.870 --> 00:09:24.220
And a very useful goal

00:09:24.220 --> 00:09:29.180
that several extensive reading programs in different schools use,

00:09:29.180 --> 00:09:32.260
is to set a goal of 1 million words.

00:09:32.260 --> 00:09:36.500
To read a few books until you reach 1 million words.

00:09:36.500 --> 00:09:40.820
When you finish reading 1 million words you will really notice

00:09:40.820 --> 00:09:47.060
that you have greatly improved your ability to read in the language.

00:09:47.060 --> 00:09:50.580
And as a final goal, as a final goal to read

00:09:50.580 --> 00:09:54.840
you can set the goal of 3 million words.

00:09:54.840 --> 00:10:01.960
In several schools I've seen, when the students read 3 million words

00:10:01.960 --> 00:10:06.929
they already reach the level where they can basically read anything,

00:10:06.929 --> 00:10:10.540
basically any book of any subject

00:10:10.540 --> 00:10:13.920
that they want to read about, they can read it and understand it well.

00:10:13.920 --> 00:10:17.280
So, I recommend that you keep a list

00:10:17.280 --> 00:10:21.380
with the name of the book you have read, and if you want also the date

00:10:21.380 --> 00:10:23.160
when you finished it,

00:10:23.160 --> 00:10:26.520
and how many words the book has.

00:10:26.520 --> 00:10:31.680
And that you them up, that you add up the number of words so that you can see that you are getting closer

00:10:31.680 --> 00:10:34.680
to your goal, that you are getting closer to your target.

00:10:34.680 --> 00:10:38.420
And that's it. This is the end of the *video about reading.

00:10:38.420 --> 00:10:43.720
In the next *video I will show you something else you can do

00:10:43.720 --> 00:10:47.720
besides Dreaming Spanish or watching other videos

00:10:47.720 --> 00:10:52.800
which is Crosstalk. It's a way of doing language exchange

00:10:52.800 --> 00:10:58.940
that I think works even faster than Dreaming Spanish. I think that it's really

00:10:58.940 --> 00:11:02.300
the activity with which you can improve

00:11:02.300 --> 00:11:07.080
in a language in the fastest way and you can learn even from zero.

00:11:07.080 --> 00:11:09.750
Okay? Alright,

00:11:09.750 --> 00:11:12.170
Bye!

title: How to Learn a Language #7: Crosstalk – A Better Way of Doing Language Exchange
description: The idea of comprehensible input really shows how silly the traditional way of doing language exchange is. In this video we introduce a more fun, less stressful, and more effective way of doing language exchange.
subtitles:
WEBVTT
Kind: captions
Language: en

00:00:00.800 --> 00:00:01.880
Hi!

00:00:01.880 --> 00:00:05.400
This is the video about Crosstalk.

00:00:05.400 --> 00:00:09.480
I have decided to talk about Crosstalk

00:00:09.480 --> 00:00:11.940
also in this series of videos

00:00:11.940 --> 00:00:16.300
because I really believe that it is the best way, the fastest way,

00:00:16.300 --> 00:00:20.020
to learn a language and to get better at a language.

00:00:20.020 --> 00:00:23.720
And you can use Crosstalk for Spanish

00:00:23.720 --> 00:00:26.480
or for any language you are learning.

00:00:26.480 --> 00:00:29.140
You just need to meet people.

00:00:29.140 --> 00:00:34.580
Find speakers, native speakers if you want.

00:00:34.580 --> 00:00:38.060
I also have a video about Crosstalk

00:00:38.060 --> 00:00:41.840
on my channel, in Spanish. I talk about Crosstalk,

00:00:41.840 --> 00:00:44.720
and I talk in more detail. You can watch that video

00:00:44.720 --> 00:00:48.200
if you want more information about how to do Crosstalk.

00:00:48.200 --> 00:00:53.100
But also on my personal channel, on the YouTube channel that has my name,

00:00:53.100 --> 00:00:56.440
I have a video in which I show it.

00:00:56.440 --> 00:00:58.920
I explain in English how Crosstalk is done

00:00:58.920 --> 00:01:01.540
and I also show it. I have a demonstration

00:01:01.540 --> 00:01:05.460
in which I speak Japanese and my friend speaks Polish to me.

00:01:05.460 --> 00:01:10.760
We are both starting from zero in the language, but we can have a conversation.

00:01:10.760 --> 00:01:14.440
So if you go to my channel, to the Crosstalk video,

00:01:14.440 --> 00:01:16.120
you will find a link.

00:01:16.120 --> 00:01:20.000
There is a link to the video in which I explain Crosstalk,

00:01:20.000 --> 00:01:22.560
in which I also demonstrate it.

00:01:22.560 --> 00:01:24.820
So, what is Crosstalk?

00:01:24.820 --> 00:01:28.780
Crosstalk is a type of language exchange.

00:01:28.780 --> 00:01:31.200
Language exchange, or tandem,

00:01:31.200 --> 00:01:33.760
is when we have a partner

00:01:33.760 --> 00:01:39.360
and we have a conversation to practice a language, to improve in a language.

00:01:39.360 --> 00:01:44.060
With Crosstalk we can be two people or we can be more, we can be a group.

00:01:44.060 --> 00:01:47.140
But the idea of Crosstalk is very different

00:01:47.140 --> 00:01:50.280
to that of other language exchanges.

00:01:50.280 --> 00:01:53.100
In many language exchanges

00:01:53.100 --> 00:01:58.740
you spend half the time speaking one language and half the time speaking the other language.

00:01:58.740 --> 00:02:03.320
Maybe ten minutes speaking one language and ten minutes speaking the other.

00:02:03.320 --> 00:02:07.140
And many people go to language exchanges

00:02:07.140 --> 00:02:10.440
​​because they want to practice, they want to

00:02:10.440 --> 00:02:14.400
practice speaking. They want the other person to correct their mistakes,

00:02:14.400 --> 00:02:15.840
to correct their problems.

00:02:15.840 --> 00:02:18.820
But Crosstalk is very different. In Crosstalk

00:02:18.820 --> 00:02:22.420
you don't practice speaking the language you are learning,

00:02:22.420 --> 00:02:24.480
because speaking is not input.

00:02:24.480 --> 00:02:27.740
You are not picking up new information.

00:02:27.740 --> 00:02:29.920
You are not learning anything new.

00:02:29.920 --> 00:02:34.460
In Crosstalk you only listen to the language you are learning

00:02:34.460 --> 00:02:39.500
and you only speak the language that the other person is learning.

00:02:39.500 --> 00:02:43.440
So, if I speak Spanish and I want to learn Chinese,

00:02:43.440 --> 00:02:46.260
I would speak Spanish to a Chinese person,

00:02:46.260 --> 00:02:49.720
because the Chinese person is learning Spanish,

00:02:49.720 --> 00:02:54.220
and the Chinese person would speak Chinese to me, because I am learning Chinese.

00:02:54.220 --> 00:02:57.100
Then you only speak the language,

00:02:57.100 --> 00:03:02.580
your native language, or the language that you speak well and that the other person is learning.

00:03:02.580 --> 00:03:05.920
The thing is, this is much more efficient

00:03:05.920 --> 00:03:09.500
than a regular language exchange,

00:03:09.500 --> 00:03:14.620
because in a language exchange you are only listening to the other person

00:03:14.620 --> 00:03:17.900
speak to you in their language half the time.

00:03:17.900 --> 00:03:20.560
Only 50% of the time.

00:03:20.560 --> 00:03:24.920
And of that 50% there is still time in which you are speaking.

00:03:24.920 --> 00:03:29.040
You have to take away another, hopefully, another 50%, right?

00:03:29.040 --> 00:03:34.580
Actually, of all the time you're there, only a quarter of the time you're listening,

00:03:34.580 --> 00:03:37.660
you're getting new information.

00:03:37.660 --> 00:03:42.160
With Crosstalk, half the time you are speaking in your language

00:03:42.160 --> 00:03:46.020
and half the time the other person is speaking in their language.

00:03:46.020 --> 00:03:50.700
Therefore you really get twice as much time listening

00:03:50.700 --> 00:03:55.000
to the language you are learning. And why do I think that Crosstalk

00:03:55.000 --> 00:03:59.920
is much more efficient than listening to Dreaming Spanish?

00:03:59.920 --> 00:04:01.620
For a number of reasons.

00:04:01.620 --> 00:04:05.400
The first reason is that with Crosstalk you will understand better

00:04:05.400 --> 00:04:08.300
what the other person is telling you,

00:04:08.300 --> 00:04:10.980
because the other person is looking at your face,

00:04:10.980 --> 00:04:14.960
the other person knows if you understand or not,

00:04:14.960 --> 00:04:18.840
and if you do not understand then they can explain it more easily.

00:04:18.840 --> 00:04:21.260
That can make it easier to understand.

00:04:21.260 --> 00:04:25.320
Another reason is that with Crosstalk

00:04:25.320 --> 00:04:28.220
you are listening to a person who is talking to you.

00:04:28.220 --> 00:04:30.020
The other person

00:04:30.020 --> 00:04:35.440
expects you to pay attention, that you pay attention to what they are telling you.

00:04:35.440 --> 00:04:40.000
It's something that's important to them. So, you have to pay attention.

00:04:40.000 --> 00:04:44.520
It's not like a video. In a video, if you are thinking about something else

00:04:44.520 --> 00:04:49.060
and don't pay attention for a minute, nothing happens, nobody gets angry.

00:04:49.060 --> 00:04:53.620
I don't know. If you don't pay attention to my video, I don't know, nothing happens.

00:04:53.620 --> 00:04:59.100
But with Crosstalk you have to pay attention because you are having a conversation.

00:04:59.100 --> 00:05:06.080
Also what the other person is telling you is more important to your life. It's more relevant to your life,

00:05:06.080 --> 00:05:10.080
because it's a friend. A friend is talking to you, is telling you things.

00:05:10.080 --> 00:05:15.260
Probably things that interest you because you may have asked them a question,

00:05:15.260 --> 00:05:18.180
you asked them something you really want to know.

00:05:18.180 --> 00:05:21.740
So, to start doing Crosstalk

00:05:21.740 --> 00:05:25.260
if you are a beginner in the language or if you start from zero

00:05:25.260 --> 00:05:28.660
is to do it the same way as my superbeginner videos.

00:05:28.660 --> 00:05:32.280
Like the videos in which I draw, in which I do gestures.

00:05:32.280 --> 00:05:34.780
You can start having a conversation

00:05:34.780 --> 00:05:38.620
in which the two people doing that, the two people draw

00:05:38.620 --> 00:05:40.640
to be able to communicate

00:05:40.640 --> 00:05:44.360
even if you don't understand anything about the other person's language.

00:05:44.360 --> 00:05:48.840
If you watch the demonstration that I put on my channel, on my personal channel,

00:05:48.840 --> 00:05:54.100
you will see how it works. It's basically the same thing I do here in my

00:05:54.100 --> 00:05:57.020
superbeginner and beginner videos but

00:05:57.020 --> 00:06:01.240
having a conversation. Instead of a single person

00:06:01.240 --> 00:06:03.740
talking about a subject, you have a conversation.

00:06:03.740 --> 00:06:06.480
At the beginning I recommend doing it in person,

00:06:06.480 --> 00:06:11.660
but when your level gets to a high beginner or intermediate,

00:06:11.660 --> 00:06:13.880
you can start using Skype

00:06:13.880 --> 00:06:16.360
and this will allow you to talk to people

00:06:16.360 --> 00:06:19.620
who are on the other side of the planet, people who live far away.

00:06:19.620 --> 00:06:23.000
And it will be easier for you to find people who speak the language.

00:06:23.000 --> 00:06:26.820
You can also prepare laminated sheets,

00:06:26.820 --> 00:06:29.360
laminated sheets like the ones I have,

00:06:29.360 --> 00:06:33.660
with maps, with drawings of fruits and vegetables,

00:06:33.660 --> 00:06:35.200
with a calendar.

00:06:35.200 --> 00:06:41.080
All the sheets I have can be used to do Crosstalk and to make it easier for you.

00:06:41.080 --> 00:06:43.240
To make it easy to point to things,

00:06:43.240 --> 00:06:46.820
maybe it's easier than drawing in many cases.

00:06:46.820 --> 00:06:51.920
And well, that's it, this is a bit of an introduction to Crosstalk.

00:06:51.920 --> 00:06:55.660
If you want to know more about the details, about how to do it,

00:06:55.660 --> 00:06:58.900
you can watch the video I have at Dreaming Spanish, on my channel.

00:06:58.900 --> 00:07:03.000
Search Crosstalk and you will find the video in which I explain more.

00:07:03.000 --> 00:07:08.460
And that's it. I really thing Crosstalk is the fastest way to learn a language.

00:07:08.460 --> 00:07:11.980
When I really want to improve quickly in a language

00:07:11.980 --> 00:07:15.560
I try to do Crosstalk, if I can, two hours a day,

00:07:15.560 --> 00:07:18.440
and if I can one day do four hours I really try to do it

00:07:18.440 --> 00:07:22.200
because I really believe that it is the most efficient, fastest way

00:07:22.200 --> 00:07:24.020
to improve in a language.

00:07:24.020 --> 00:07:26.320
And that's it. Here ends the video.

00:07:26.320 --> 00:07:31.060
In the following videos I will tell you how to continue learning a language

00:07:31.060 --> 00:07:33.600
with immersion. Immersing in

00:07:33.600 --> 00:07:38.320
content for natives, in content

00:07:38.320 --> 00:07:42.520
of the country where the language you want to learn is spoken,

00:07:42.520 --> 00:07:45.500
and then also a video

00:07:45.500 --> 00:07:48.240
about how to continue learning the language

00:07:48.240 --> 00:07:53.320
once you go to live in the country, once you are already living in the country

00:07:53.320 --> 00:07:56.040
where the language is spoken. Okay?

00:07:56.040 --> 00:07:58.160
Alright, see you later!

description: Have more questions that weren’t addressed in the previous videos? We answer some frequently asked questions here.
subtitles:
WEBVTT
Kind: captions
Language: en

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:02.000
Hello!

00:00:02.000 --> 00:00:08.140
In this course about the best way to learn Spanish

00:00:08.140 --> 00:00:12.080
there were several topics that I wanted to talk about.

00:00:12.080 --> 00:00:16.420
I wanted to talk about many things, many details.

00:00:16.420 --> 00:00:21.900
And I thought that it would be a good idea to make a video of questions and answers.

00:00:21.900 --> 00:00:29.520
So, in this video I'm going to tell you questions that I receive frequently,

00:00:29.520 --> 00:00:34.680
that people ask often, and I will answer those questions.

00:00:34.680 --> 00:00:37.940
So you can learn too.

00:00:37.940 --> 00:00:43.700
So, this video is the first part of the questions and answers video.

00:00:43.700 --> 00:00:45.300
Let's start.

00:00:45.300 --> 00:00:50.080
The first question or comment I receive often

00:00:50.080 --> 00:00:56.060
is that sometimes people tell me they don't understand everything

00:00:56.060 --> 00:00:59.280
I say in my videos, they don't understand everything.

00:00:59.280 --> 00:01:02.760
And yes, that's the idea. The idea is that in order to learn

00:01:02.760 --> 00:01:04.600
we don't understand everything.

00:01:04.600 --> 00:01:08.100
We have to find new things that we still don't understand

00:01:08.100 --> 00:01:10.720
to be able to learn them, right?

00:01:10.720 --> 00:01:15.920
And it's true that in the other video, in the video about

00:01:15.920 --> 00:01:19.020
how to watch Dreaming Spanish videos,

00:01:19.020 --> 00:01:23.180
I explain that it's much better to watch videos that are easy,

00:01:23.180 --> 00:01:26.900
even that seem too easy.

00:01:26.900 --> 00:01:33.060
But at the start, when you are watching beginner or superbeginner videos

00:01:33.060 --> 00:01:39.840
your Spanish is not good enough to find videos

00:01:39.840 --> 00:01:43.140
that are too easy, right? So,

00:01:43.140 --> 00:01:48.660
it's normal that at the beginning there are many words that you don't understand,

00:01:48.660 --> 00:01:54.060
but the important thing is that you understand the topic, that you understand the story.

00:01:54.060 --> 00:01:59.620
If you understand the subject, the story, if you understand a few of the sentences

00:01:59.620 --> 00:02:04.500
I'm saying, it's not necessary to understand each word.

00:02:04.500 --> 00:02:10.680
But you can start to understand what some words mean,

00:02:10.680 --> 00:02:14.380
especially words that refer to things, right? To objects.

00:02:14.380 --> 00:02:17.720
Cellphone, paper, right?

00:02:17.720 --> 00:02:20.880
Different objects that I show in the videos.

00:02:20.880 --> 00:02:24.180
You can start learning those words

00:02:24.180 --> 00:02:27.840
and that's it. That is all you need

00:02:27.840 --> 00:02:31.860
to keep improving, to be able to learn the language.

00:02:31.860 --> 00:02:35.680
So don't worry if you don't understand everything,

00:02:35.680 --> 00:02:39.800
because you aren't going to understand everything for a long time.

00:02:39.800 --> 00:02:43.920
There are some words, especially words

00:02:43.920 --> 00:02:48.700
that only have a function, that have no clear meaning,

00:02:48.700 --> 00:02:51.060
that are grammatical words,

00:02:51.060 --> 00:02:53.360
that are learned later.

00:02:53.360 --> 00:02:56.800
You have to understand already many words

00:02:56.800 --> 00:03:01.120
to begin to understand the meaning of these words,

00:03:01.120 --> 00:03:03.260
of these grammatical words.

00:03:03.260 --> 00:03:07.640
So, if you don't understand everything, if you don't understand all the words,

00:03:07.640 --> 00:03:13.720
Don't worry. Try to watch the easiest videos you can find.

00:03:13.720 --> 00:03:19.740
And it will be enough to keep learning vocabulary, to keep learning Spanish.

00:03:19.740 --> 00:03:24.680
Another related question that people ask me, or comment, is:

00:03:24.680 --> 00:03:30.140
"I don't understand anything. Even in the easiest videos I don't understand anything."

00:03:30.140 --> 00:03:37.840
Okay, I think we have a different idea of ​​what it means to understand and to not understand.

00:03:37.840 --> 00:03:43.660
When many people say "I don't understand anything," they mean:

00:03:43.660 --> 00:03:48.240
"I'm not one hundred percent sure of anything."

00:03:48.240 --> 00:03:51.980
And yes, it's normal. When you start learning a language

00:03:51.980 --> 00:03:59.340
It's normal that you're not 100% sure of the meaning, maybe of the meaning of any phrase.

00:03:59.340 --> 00:04:04.720
But it's not necessary, it's not necessary. That's not the idea of ​​Dreaming Spanish.

00:04:04.720 --> 00:04:08.640
That's not the idea of ​​learning with Comprehensible Input.

00:04:08.640 --> 00:04:13.800
If I say to you the word "paper", and I show you a sheet of paper,

00:04:13.800 --> 00:04:17.800
and later on I talk about something else and paper,

00:04:17.800 --> 00:04:22.340
eventually your brain will directly relate

00:04:22.340 --> 00:04:26.520
the word "paper" with the sheet of paper,

00:04:26.520 --> 00:04:29.940
and that there isn't anyone who doesn't understand that.

00:04:29.940 --> 00:04:34.140
In my videos at beginner, superbeginner, especially in superbeginner,

00:04:34.140 --> 00:04:37.760
there are enough occasions where I say words

00:04:37.760 --> 00:04:40.180
and I show directly what it is.

00:04:40.180 --> 00:04:43.080
And with repetition you will understand.

00:04:43.080 --> 00:04:48.320
It's not necessary to understand one hundred percent of any phrase, of whole sentences

00:04:48.320 --> 00:04:52.000
at the beginning, because it is not possible.

00:04:52.000 --> 00:04:58.260
So, just understand that the important thing is

00:04:58.260 --> 00:05:03.040
to understand the topic, the story,
the general topic I'm talking about.

00:05:03.040 --> 00:05:05.580
And thanks to that you can start

00:05:05.580 --> 00:05:09.880
to learn concrete words,
single words at the beginning.

00:05:09.880 --> 00:05:13.260
Another question I received many times is:

00:05:13.260 --> 00:05:17.720
"What is the best level of videos for me?"

00:05:17.720 --> 00:05:22.600
The best level is the level at which you don't get bored

00:05:22.600 --> 00:05:28.720
and that is the easiest one, the easiest one
you can tolerate, at which you don't get bored.

00:05:28.720 --> 00:05:32.860
The easiest that you still find interesting, and fun.

00:05:34.800 --> 00:05:39.060
Some level may be too easy.

00:05:39.060 --> 00:05:44.460
If you really watch an entire video and there is no word

00:05:44.460 --> 00:05:47.740
that you didn't know, if you already know all of them.

00:05:47.740 --> 00:05:51.240
Then yes, it might be a bit too easy.

00:05:51.240 --> 00:05:56.980
But even if there are as few as four or five words that you don't know

00:05:56.980 --> 00:06:01.800
you are already learning, and you are surely learning faster

00:06:01.800 --> 00:06:05.800
than if there are 20 or 30 words you don't know in the video.

00:06:05.800 --> 00:06:10.000
So, in general, I recommend watching videos

00:06:10.000 --> 00:06:14.140
that are a little easier than you think you should watch.

00:06:14.140 --> 00:06:19.900
Another question is: "Should I watch a video several times or many times?"

00:06:19.920 --> 00:06:23.240
And I answer this question in more detail

00:06:23.240 --> 00:06:29.160
in the video about how to watch the videos, about how to use Dreaming Spanish.

00:06:29.160 --> 00:06:31.700
I recommend watching that video.

00:06:31.700 --> 00:06:34.320
In short,

00:06:34.320 --> 00:06:38.980
you don't have to force yourself to watch a video several times,

00:06:38.980 --> 00:06:42.340
especially don't watch a video several times

00:06:42.340 --> 00:06:47.960
if you start to get bored, if you notice that, since you already know the video,

00:06:47.960 --> 00:06:51.280
you are getting bored, you are not paying attention.

00:06:51.280 --> 00:06:55.600
It's better to watch a new video, a video about some subject that interests you.

00:06:55.600 --> 00:06:58.840
But if the video doesn't bore you yet,

00:06:58.840 --> 00:07:02.640
if you watched it long ago and you want to watch it again,

00:07:02.640 --> 00:07:04.380
to see if you now understand more,

00:07:04.380 --> 00:07:07.660
then yes. You can do it. There is no problem.

00:07:07.660 --> 00:07:13.120
Another question is: "Should I try to memorize words?"

00:07:13.120 --> 00:07:14.160
No.

00:07:14.160 --> 00:07:17.900
The method of learning with Comprehensible Input

00:07:17.900 --> 00:07:22.300
does not require memorizing words.

00:07:22.300 --> 00:07:27.700
If you hear a word you don't know, you don't have to repeat it in your head:

00:07:27.700 --> 00:07:33.380
"boli, boli, boli, boli, boli." No, it's not necessary. And it's not really useful.

00:07:33.380 --> 00:07:37.920
It's better to pay attention to the video,
to listen to what's happening,

00:07:37.920 --> 00:07:42.560
and the word "boli" will appear later in another context,

00:07:42.560 --> 00:07:46.060
in another situation, said by other people,

00:07:46.060 --> 00:07:50.000
and that will help us more to learn the word "boli"

00:07:50.000 --> 00:07:54.380
and to learn all its meaning and the ways it is used.

00:07:54.380 --> 00:08:00.000
Much more than repeating in your head
the word: "boli, boli, boli...", constantly.

00:08:00.000 --> 00:08:04.640
So no, don't try to memorize certain words.

00:08:04.640 --> 00:08:09.060
Trust that if you receive a lot of input, you listen to a lot of Spanish,

00:08:09.060 --> 00:08:14.180
the words are going to get repeated because if they are useful you will hear them again, for sure.

00:08:14.180 --> 00:08:19.480
Another question is: "Should I use a dictionary?"

00:08:19.480 --> 00:08:26.600
In general no, I do not recommend using a dictionary in almost any situation.

00:08:26.600 --> 00:08:31.500
In general I think that dictionaries are used too much,

00:08:31.500 --> 00:08:34.840
and they are not so useful to learn a language .

00:08:34.840 --> 00:08:40.020
A case in which I especially do not recommend using dictionary

00:08:40.020 --> 00:08:44.360
it's if you are listening to Spanish, or you are reading Spanish,

00:08:44.360 --> 00:08:47.360
and you see a word you don't know.

00:08:47.360 --> 00:08:50.360
Especially a word that's not very important.

00:08:50.360 --> 00:08:55.380
Then, no. Look it up in the dictionary... You will look at the definition

00:08:55.380 --> 00:09:00.320
and after 5 minutes you will forget the word and the meaning.

00:09:00.320 --> 00:09:05.660
The only situation in which consulting a dictionary

00:09:05.660 --> 00:09:10.080
I think makes sense and it's not bad

00:09:10.080 --> 00:09:14.440
it's if you're listening to a video or reading something

00:09:14.440 --> 00:09:18.200
and you see that the same word is repeated over and over,

00:09:18.200 --> 00:09:22.700
and knowing this word is important to understand

00:09:22.700 --> 00:09:25.060
the story or to understand the video.

00:09:25.060 --> 00:09:28.000
If you realize that: "If I don't know this word

00:09:28.000 --> 00:09:30.000
I don't understand anything here",

00:09:30.000 --> 00:09:35.820
Well, one option is to watch another video, and that option is still possible. There is nothing wrong

00:09:35.820 --> 00:09:39.300
in saying: "okay, I'm going to watch an easier video".

00:09:39.300 --> 00:09:44.960
But if you are watching a series or reading a book,

00:09:44.960 --> 00:09:50.460
and you want to understand that part, that portion of the book or series,

00:09:50.460 --> 00:09:53.920
and you need to understand that word, then in that case

00:09:53.920 --> 00:09:58.900
I think that yes, there's no problem in consulting the dictionary.

00:09:58.900 --> 00:10:04.020
Use the dictionary only to understand the word in that context,

00:10:04.020 --> 00:10:08.860
to find what can that be in that context, what can it mean.

00:10:08.860 --> 00:10:12.320
But you have to let the meaning

00:10:12.320 --> 00:10:15.560
of the word to be given by the context, given by the book,

00:10:15.560 --> 00:10:17.880
or given by the TV series,

00:10:17.880 --> 00:10:21.780
not the dictionary. The dictionary will give you several options,

00:10:21.780 --> 00:10:25.920
but there's no point in trying to memorize those words,

00:10:25.920 --> 00:10:30.440
because the dictionary is not telling you in what situation

00:10:30.440 --> 00:10:32.960
you can use each word, in what situations,

00:10:32.960 --> 00:10:38.560
especially, in what situations you cannot use each word, each translation.

00:10:39.540 --> 00:10:43.320
So, use the dictionary only as a clue

00:10:43.320 --> 00:10:46.060
to help you understand the meaning,

00:10:46.060 --> 00:10:49.560
this meaning, of this word in this context.

00:10:49.560 --> 00:10:53.540
Is it better to watch videos with or without subtitles?

00:10:53.540 --> 00:10:58.340
Because I know there are many people who watch Dreaming Spanish with subtitles.

00:10:58.340 --> 00:11:03.820
I recommend never watching videos with English subtitles,

00:11:03.820 --> 00:11:07.280
with subtitles that are not in the same language, that's for sure.

00:11:07.280 --> 00:11:11.660
Because your head is in English mode, it's not in Spanish mode.

00:11:11.660 --> 00:11:18.060
Then, whether I recommend or not to watch them with Spanish subtitles.

00:11:18.060 --> 00:11:25.040
On this issue I have not yet made a clear decision. I am not 100% sure

00:11:25.040 --> 00:11:27.060
which is the best way.

00:11:27.060 --> 00:11:30.980
If you haven't read much Spanish, you haven't practiced reading much,

00:11:30.980 --> 00:11:34.320
If you are starting to learn Spanish with Dreaming Spanish,

00:11:34.320 --> 00:11:38.180
then remove the subtitles. The subtitles are not going to help you much.

00:11:38.180 --> 00:11:42.860
For people who studied Spanish at school, first, who normally

00:11:42.860 --> 00:11:46.680
are forced to read a lot and use written Spanish a lot,

00:11:46.680 --> 00:11:53.560
I understand that it helps you to identify the words, to know what words I'm saying.

00:11:53.560 --> 00:11:58.520
I don't know if it's very useful, because it can distract you, it can cause you

00:11:58.520 --> 00:12:02.620
to be reading and be a bit ignoring

00:12:02.620 --> 00:12:07.060
what I'm saying, or what I'm really talking about, right?

00:12:07.060 --> 00:12:12.940
It may be that while reading you are also using the sounds of Spanish

00:12:12.940 --> 00:12:14.960
that you have in your head,

00:12:14.960 --> 00:12:18.600
which can be sounds of English, they can be sounds of another language,

00:12:18.600 --> 00:12:22.440
not really the Spanish sounds that I'm using.

00:12:22.440 --> 00:12:28.320
That's why I am not sure that it's best to watch with subtitles on.

00:12:28.320 --> 00:12:32.560
But I still don't have a clear answer to this question.

00:12:32.560 --> 00:12:33.660
I'm not sure yet.

00:12:33.660 --> 00:12:38.260
Another question is: "Okay Pablo, I've already seen all your videos

00:12:38.260 --> 00:12:41.840
and now I don't know what else to do. "

00:12:41.840 --> 00:12:45.040
Well, there are many things you can do.

00:12:45.040 --> 00:12:49.820
I recommend that you watch the other videos of this course because I explain how

00:12:49.820 --> 00:12:54.720
to get immersion, how to get immersion in

00:12:54.720 --> 00:12:59.000
content for natives and content for learners.

00:12:59.000 --> 00:13:04.020
In that video I also recommend several podcasts.

00:13:04.020 --> 00:13:06.080
Also crosstalk.

00:13:06.080 --> 00:13:10.340
And also immersion if you live in the country where the language is spoken.

00:13:10.340 --> 00:13:13.180
Different ways how you can get immersion.

00:13:13.180 --> 00:13:15.420
Well, for each of these three things,

00:13:15.420 --> 00:13:19.440
there is a video in this same course and I recommend that you watch them.

00:13:19.440 --> 00:13:23.780
Another question that I've been asked many times is:

00:13:23.780 --> 00:13:30.260
"Pablo, I understand your videos, I understand your intermediate, advanced videos,

00:13:30.260 --> 00:13:33.580
but I don't understand movies and TV series

00:13:33.580 --> 00:13:37.000
or youtubers. I don't understand other Spaniards

00:13:37.000 --> 00:13:40.100
or Spanish speakers when they speak.

00:13:40.100 --> 00:13:46.080
They speak too fast, or do not pronounce clearly, etc".

00:13:46.080 --> 00:13:48.260
Okay

00:13:48.260 --> 00:13:52.380
Sure, you understand me better because I'm making videos

00:13:52.380 --> 00:13:54.520
For people who learn Spanish.

00:13:54.520 --> 00:13:59.300
Because I pronounce clearly. I try. I try to pronounce clearly.

00:13:59.300 --> 00:14:04.260
Many times I don't speak too fast, I don't speak as fast

00:14:04.260 --> 00:14:08.820
as I would when I talk to my friends or my family.

00:14:08.820 --> 00:14:13.940
But also very important is that I talk about a subject

00:14:13.940 --> 00:14:16.760
in a continued way. I talk about a subject continuously.

00:14:16.760 --> 00:14:18.520
I start talking about a topic

00:14:18.520 --> 00:14:21.760
and you already know more or less what to expect,

00:14:21.760 --> 00:14:27.120
what things can exist within this subject, within this context, right?

00:14:27.120 --> 00:14:30.120
When you watch a TV series or watch a movie,

00:14:30.120 --> 00:14:32.660
and there is a change of context,

00:14:32.660 --> 00:14:37.220
people start to have another conversation, to talk about a different topic.

00:14:37.220 --> 00:14:41.120
When you watch a youtuber, who tells you a joke

00:14:41.120 --> 00:14:43.840
or uses many colloquial expressions,

00:14:43.840 --> 00:14:48.820
uses many idioms, right? With figurative meanings.

00:14:48.820 --> 00:14:52.300
And in general the way I recommend to address this is:

00:14:52.300 --> 00:14:56.900
first to keep watching Dreaming Spanish or other videos

00:14:56.900 --> 00:15:01.140
or intermediate podcasts,

00:15:01.140 --> 00:15:06.440
because you are going to get more and more vocabulary, you are going to learn more and more vocabulary.

00:15:06.440 --> 00:15:10.140
And knowing a lot of vocabulary, knowing many words,

00:15:10.140 --> 00:15:16.340
will help you with those changes of subject, with those changes of context.

00:15:16.340 --> 00:15:19.280
Because when there is a change of context

00:15:19.280 --> 00:15:22.160
you have to understand very well the following words

00:15:22.160 --> 00:15:25.040
they say, the first words they say.

00:15:25.040 --> 00:15:28.520
To understand: "OK, they're talking about that topic," right?

00:15:28.520 --> 00:15:31.500
So, you need a lot of vocabulary.

00:15:31.500 --> 00:15:34.160
Also a lot of practice listening,

00:15:34.160 --> 00:15:37.900
because if you studied Spanish at school before

00:15:37.900 --> 00:15:41.600
or have you studied with books, you have learned

00:15:41.600 --> 00:15:44.400
many words perhaps as translations,

00:15:44.400 --> 00:15:46.400
or you have learned to read them,

00:15:46.400 --> 00:15:50.400
but you need to get used to hearing them and hearing them many times

00:15:50.400 --> 00:15:53.880
so you can identify them faster.

00:15:53.880 --> 00:15:57.160
You really need to hear them and connect

00:15:57.160 --> 00:16:00.820
directly the word with the meaning

00:16:00.820 --> 00:16:05.600
and then be able to identify it, be able to understand it very quickly

00:16:05.600 --> 00:16:07.900
when a person speaks quickly,

00:16:07.900 --> 00:16:12.680
or also when a person doesn't pronounce clearly.

00:16:12.680 --> 00:16:16.980
When they don't pronounce clearly, if on top of that

00:16:16.980 --> 00:16:21.680
you still don't know very well the words they say,

00:16:21.680 --> 00:16:24.020
it's hard for you to identify them.

00:16:24.020 --> 00:16:27.740
While if you already know the words well,

00:16:27.740 --> 00:16:30.060
as soon as you hear something that sounds similar

00:16:30.060 --> 00:16:36.640
it will be easier for you and faster for you to know what they're saying.

00:16:36.640 --> 00:16:42.980
And of course practice listening to people who don't speak that clearly,

00:16:42.980 --> 00:16:45.700
who talk maybe a little faster.

00:16:45.700 --> 00:16:50.400
And that, with my advanced level videos I'm trying to do something like that.

00:16:50.400 --> 00:16:55.420
And in the future I think I will try to find more people, more teachers,

00:16:55.420 --> 00:16:58.000
to make videos for Dreaming Spanish

00:16:58.000 --> 00:17:02.320
so you get used to different ways of pronouncing words.

00:17:02.320 --> 00:17:07.000
Okay. The following are two related questions.

00:17:07.000 --> 00:17:11.900
The first one is: "Pablo, why do I understand you?

00:17:11.900 --> 00:17:16.020
but I don't know how to speak, or I don't know how to speak at the same level?"

00:17:16.020 --> 00:17:20.540
Or "why do I understand at a much higher level

00:17:20.540 --> 00:17:23.960
than I can really speak?"

00:17:23.960 --> 00:17:27.100
And the answer is yes.

00:17:27.100 --> 00:17:30.320
Just yes. It is like that. Everyone is like that.

00:17:30.320 --> 00:17:32.620
Native speakers are like that.

00:17:32.620 --> 00:17:37.100
We understand many many more words than we use.

00:17:37.100 --> 00:17:42.140
Many more words than we can use. Even if we try,

00:17:42.140 --> 00:17:46.420
there are many words, words that we have seen a few times,

00:17:46.420 --> 00:17:48.320
that we have only read,

00:17:48.320 --> 00:17:51.180
that if we tried to remember them

00:17:51.180 --> 00:17:55.200
they wouldn't come out, or it would be hard for us to remember those words.

00:17:55.200 --> 00:17:56.660
MANY more.

00:17:56.660 --> 00:18:00.340
So, this is something that cannot be avoided.

00:18:00.340 --> 00:18:03.980
A word, to understand it, we have to

00:18:03.980 --> 00:18:08.000
know it at this level, but to use it

00:18:08.000 --> 00:18:10.180
we have to know it at this level.

00:18:10.180 --> 00:18:13.240
Therefore, there will always be many words

00:18:13.240 --> 00:18:17.620
that are not yet at this level, that we have to keep improving.

00:18:17.620 --> 00:18:21.640
There will always be more words that are at least here,

00:18:21.640 --> 00:18:25.040
than words that are at least here, right?

00:18:25.040 --> 00:18:28.200
And yes, you have to get used to it because it's inevitable.

00:18:28.200 --> 00:18:33.860
Think about how it also happens to you in your own language.

00:18:33.860 --> 00:18:39.180
So, to be able to speak a language fluently

00:18:39.180 --> 00:18:43.440
what you have to do is not to get all the words

00:18:43.440 --> 00:18:46.880
that you know at this level reach this level, no.

00:18:46.880 --> 00:18:50.260
You have to keep improving all the words,

00:18:50.260 --> 00:18:55.640
improving all of them so that the number of words that are at this level

00:18:55.640 --> 00:18:59.380
is enough, enough to talk

00:18:59.380 --> 00:19:03.660
about any topic you may want to talk about during your daily life.

00:19:03.660 --> 00:19:06.720
Another question or complaint is:

00:19:06.720 --> 00:19:10.920
"Pablo, I make mistakes often, I make many errors."

00:19:10.920 --> 00:19:15.600
Well, this question is related to the previous one,

00:19:15.600 --> 00:19:17.800
with the fact that

00:19:17.800 --> 00:19:22.660
when you are having a conversation you may understand the other person,

00:19:22.660 --> 00:19:26.880
but when we try to say something you make a mistake. And there are things

00:19:26.880 --> 00:19:31.620
that you may understand, there are past tenses or the subjunctive

00:19:31.620 --> 00:19:36.880
that you understand, but when you try to use them it doesn't come out right.

00:19:36.880 --> 00:19:40.440
Or you make mistakes.

00:19:40.440 --> 00:19:47.620
Then yes. The problem is the same as in the previous question,

00:19:47.620 --> 00:19:52.560
and is that to also understand a certain grammar rule

00:19:52.560 --> 00:19:56.480
you have to reach a certain level, and to be able to use it

00:19:56.480 --> 00:20:01.280
and for it to come out naturally, then that level needs to be higher.

00:20:01.280 --> 00:20:07.220
But the way that is achieved is with input, with exposure to the language,

00:20:07.220 --> 00:20:11.680
listening to the language, reading the language and getting used to the language.

00:20:11.680 --> 00:20:15.580
Because if you do that a lot it will sound natural to you.

00:20:15.580 --> 00:20:19.500
It will seem natural to you and that phrase will come naturally to you

00:20:19.500 --> 00:20:20.940
well formed.

00:20:20.940 --> 00:20:25.900
And if you think about it, there are many things about the language, about Spanish,

00:20:25.900 --> 00:20:28.980
that have you learned, that you get right, that you know how to use.

00:20:28.980 --> 00:20:33.560
Then, if until now with that input you have got this far,

00:20:33.560 --> 00:20:36.640
you can continue using input and you will continue moving forward,

00:20:36.640 --> 00:20:40.020
you will keep learning more complicated grammar.

00:20:40.020 --> 00:20:45.320
If input has already worked for you for certain easier grammar

00:20:45.320 --> 00:20:49.100
then it will continue working for more complicated grammar,

00:20:49.100 --> 00:20:52.720
Because in the end it's all the same. There is nothing that's

00:20:52.720 --> 00:20:56.520
fundamentally different between simpler grammar

00:20:56.520 --> 00:21:00.700
and more complicated grammar, more advanced I would say.

00:21:00.700 --> 00:21:03.540
Well, this video is a bit long already.

00:21:03.540 --> 00:21:08.100
This is going to be the first part of questions and answers,

00:21:08.100 --> 00:21:10.420
and I'm going to do a second part,

00:21:10.420 --> 00:21:13.920
so watch the second part of this video too, okay?

00:21:13.920 --> 00:21:19.020
Alright, see you later!

title: How to Learn a Language #8: Immerse Yourself in Native Media
description: In this video we talk a little about when to start incorporating content meant for native speakers into your learning routine. What kind of native media is easier to start with?
subtitles:
WEBVTT
Kind: captions
Language: en

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:02.000
Hi!

00:00:02.000 --> 00:00:06.900
This video is about how you can continue to improve

00:00:06.900 --> 00:00:10.760
and how you can make the most of your time learning a language

00:00:10.760 --> 00:00:14.420
by immersing yourself in the language. Doing immersion

00:00:14.420 --> 00:00:18.280
in multimedia content

00:00:18.280 --> 00:00:21.840
of the language. In content for native speakers.

00:00:21.840 --> 00:00:25.960
In audios, radio, TV series, movies,

00:00:25.960 --> 00:00:28.040
videos, anything

00:00:28.040 --> 00:00:30.780
made for native speakers.

00:00:30.780 --> 00:00:36.000
So, when you start to learn a language, when you are a beginner,

00:00:36.000 --> 00:00:40.280
what I recommend is watching Dreaming Spanish

00:00:40.280 --> 00:00:44.640
or something equivalent to Dreaming Spanish, and doing Crosstalk.

00:00:44.640 --> 00:00:49.360
The last video I made was about Crosstalk, and I recommend watching it.

00:00:49.360 --> 00:00:54.360
But another way you can continue to improve in the language is

00:00:54.360 --> 00:00:56.140
by watching TV series,

00:00:56.140 --> 00:00:59.820
listening to the radio, or watching television or movies.

00:00:59.820 --> 00:01:03.360
Simply doing anything in the language.

00:01:03.360 --> 00:01:05.300
What's the issue though?

00:01:05.300 --> 00:01:11.620
That this is more useful if your level is already intermediate, perhaps even intermediate high,

00:01:11.620 --> 00:01:16.080
or advanced. Then it will be much more useful. You will

00:01:16.080 --> 00:01:21.060
learn faster. You will learn vocabulary faster, it will help you more, right?

00:01:21.060 --> 00:01:24.840
But there is also no problem with starting to listen to the language

00:01:24.840 --> 00:01:29.220
from the beginning when you are beginners or are at an intermediate level.

00:01:29.220 --> 00:01:32.540
You can start already listening to the language.

00:01:32.540 --> 00:01:36.580
You will not learn many new words,

00:01:36.580 --> 00:01:40.740
you will probably not learn any new grammar.

00:01:40.740 --> 00:01:45.620
It's more useful to get used to the rhythm of the language,

00:01:45.620 --> 00:01:49.820
to get used to the pronunciation of certain words, right?

00:01:49.820 --> 00:01:54.400
But starting at the intermediate level, then yes, it begins to be more useful

00:01:54.400 --> 00:01:58.500
and I recommend you do it. And I recommend you do as much as you can.

00:01:58.500 --> 00:02:02.100
If you can listen, listen to Spanish

00:02:02.100 --> 00:02:06.680
when you go to the toilet or when you are in the car or on the train,

00:02:06.680 --> 00:02:09.400
that is time that you can use.

00:02:09.400 --> 00:02:12.320
That's why I always wear these headphones.

00:02:12.320 --> 00:02:15.500
I have them here, ready. I can press a button

00:02:15.500 --> 00:02:19.260
and start learning the language I am learning, right?

00:02:19.260 --> 00:02:23.640
What do I recommend doing if you are at an intermediate level?

00:02:23.640 --> 00:02:25.480
When you are at the intermediate level

00:02:25.480 --> 00:02:30.180
it's still a bit difficult to understand Spanish series and movies,

00:02:30.180 --> 00:02:34.580
or to *listen to Spanish radio. I recommend that you watch videos

00:02:34.580 --> 00:02:38.580
and listen to podcasts at the intermediate level.

00:02:38.580 --> 00:02:41.840
I recommend for example Spanish with Juan,

00:02:41.840 --> 00:02:45.880
which is a YouTube channel. And his podcast too, he also has a podcast.

00:02:45.880 --> 00:02:48.920
And there are other podcasts at the intermediate level

00:02:48.920 --> 00:02:51.800
and I will put the links in the description.

00:02:51.800 --> 00:02:55.800
I will give you recommendations of podcasts that you can check out.

00:02:55.800 --> 00:03:00.600
So, at the intermediate level I recommend that you start doing that, that you start

00:03:00.600 --> 00:03:03.920
listening whenever you have the opportunity.

00:03:03.920 --> 00:03:08.180
You can also start watching cartoons.

00:03:08.180 --> 00:03:11.580
Cartoons. Cartoon series

00:03:11.580 --> 00:03:15.140
such as Peppa Pig. Peppa Pig is very easy,

00:03:15.140 --> 00:03:18.360
and cartoons of that level

00:03:18.360 --> 00:03:22.280
are perfect if you are at the intermediate level.

00:03:22.280 --> 00:03:26.800
Not all cartoons are necessarily going to be easy, though.

00:03:26.800 --> 00:03:31.140
If you are at the intermediate level there will still be many cartoons

00:03:31.140 --> 00:03:35.940
that even if they are meant for children, will still be quite difficult to understand.

00:03:35.940 --> 00:03:40.660
Once you are at a high intermediate level or at an advanced level,

00:03:40.660 --> 00:03:44.220
then you can start to consume

00:03:44.220 --> 00:03:46.260
other types of content.

00:03:46.260 --> 00:03:50.840
You can start watching easy TV series,

00:03:50.840 --> 00:03:54.840
series about families or about students.

00:03:54.840 --> 00:03:58.600
Shows about daily life, everyday life, daily life,

00:03:58.600 --> 00:04:01.140
are the shows that will be easier for you.

00:04:01.140 --> 00:04:06.420
Also talk shows, programs in which people talk about their lives,

00:04:06.420 --> 00:04:11.880
in which they interview a famous person, interview an actor or a singer, or

00:04:11.880 --> 00:04:15.260
especially if it's a person that you like.

00:04:15.260 --> 00:04:19.000
You can watch their interviews or TV shows

00:04:19.000 --> 00:04:23.880
in which this person appears. Also, once you arrive at an advanced level,

00:04:23.880 --> 00:04:29.900
you can start watching any other television series or movies,

00:04:29.900 --> 00:04:34.420
listen to podcasts or listen to radio programs for native speakers.

00:04:34.420 --> 00:04:39.260
Not necessarily for people who are learning Spanish,

00:04:39.260 --> 00:04:43.220
but the same that we native speakers of Spanish would listen to, in Spanish.

00:04:43.220 --> 00:04:45.820
Start reading novels.

00:04:45.820 --> 00:04:49.040
Novels or books. Also

00:04:49.040 --> 00:04:52.820
non-fiction books. Essay, or books

00:04:52.820 --> 00:04:57.240
about business or any other type of books that are informative,

00:04:57.240 --> 00:05:01.520
are often easier to understand than literature.

00:05:01.520 --> 00:05:04.260
And also setting your phone,

00:05:04.260 --> 00:05:08.500
your phone and your computer, to the language, setting them to Spanish,

00:05:08.500 --> 00:05:11.020
or setting them to the language you are learning,

00:05:11.020 --> 00:05:13.840
will also help you learn vocabulary

00:05:13.840 --> 00:05:17.980
for that situation, right? Computer or cellphone-related vocabulary.

00:05:17.980 --> 00:05:21.020
And of course social activities.

00:05:21.020 --> 00:05:26.480
Both social on the Internet, and subscribe to people on Twitter

00:05:26.480 --> 00:05:29.160
who tweet in Spanish,

00:05:29.160 --> 00:05:32.720
or make friends on Facebook also post in Spanish.

00:05:32.720 --> 00:05:38.920
Or just make friends and do social activities

00:05:38.920 --> 00:05:42.120
in the country. Or social activities

00:05:42.120 --> 00:05:46.400
that Spanish-speaking people, that a groups of Spanish-speaking people do, right?

00:05:46.400 --> 00:05:51.180
Well, if you like cycling, then go with a group of people who go cycling.

00:05:51.180 --> 00:05:55.860
If you like crocheting, then look for a group, I don't know, a crochet group

00:05:55.860 --> 00:05:59.120
there, where you live.

00:05:59.120 --> 00:06:01.520
Especially if you live in the country.

00:06:01.520 --> 00:06:04.420
Especially if you live in the country where the language is spoken,

00:06:04.420 --> 00:06:07.120
I recommend already at that level,

00:06:07.120 --> 00:06:10.840
intermediate level high or advanced,

00:06:10.840 --> 00:06:14.380
that you do as many social activities as you can.

00:06:14.380 --> 00:06:18.640
And that's it, this video ends here. In the next one

00:06:18.640 --> 00:06:22.620
I will give you more information about what we can do

00:06:22.620 --> 00:06:26.120
when we live in the country where the language is spoken

00:06:26.120 --> 00:06:28.780
and we want to make the most of our time.

00:06:28.780 --> 00:06:32.560
Sometimes we go only a few months, or we go only one year

00:06:32.560 --> 00:06:35.560
to the country and we want to make the most of that time

00:06:35.560 --> 00:06:40.320
learn the as fast as we can while we are in the country.

00:06:40.320 --> 00:06:44.920
Well, watch the next video to know more about this topic.

00:06:44.920 --> 00:06:47.600
Alright. See you later!
