00:00:00.520 --> 00:00:02.000
Hi!

00:00:02.000 --> 00:00:08.620
Welcome to the second part of the video about
frequently asked questions and answers.

00:00:08.640 --> 00:00:12.940
I already did a first part,
but I have many questions

00:00:12.940 --> 00:00:16.200
so this is the second part.

00:00:16.200 --> 00:00:21.820
The next question that I have also
been asked several times is:

00:00:21.820 --> 00:00:27.180
"How do I know that I am making progress?
How do I know that I am improving in the language?"

00:00:27.180 --> 00:00:31.500
For me, the best way that helps me
know that I am making progress

00:00:31.500 --> 00:00:39.460
is simply knowing that this week I understand
words that I didn't understand last week.

00:00:39.460 --> 00:00:44.900
In my experience, whenever
I make sure I keep learning words,

00:00:44.900 --> 00:00:49.580
that I know more words,
that I understand more words than last week,

00:00:49.580 --> 00:00:52.820
I realize that I have improved, that I'm improving,

00:00:52.820 --> 00:00:55.620
that I understand things that I didn't understand before.

00:00:55.620 --> 00:01:00.140
And that I can also say things that I didn't know how to say before.

00:01:00.140 --> 00:01:03.360
And you will realize that if you keep getting that input,

00:01:03.360 --> 00:01:07.900
if you listen to Spanish for a while every day, every week

00:01:07.900 --> 00:01:12.620
you are going to realize that there are words
that you can now understand that last week

00:01:12.620 --> 00:01:14.080
you couldn't understand.

00:01:14.080 --> 00:01:19.280
So, the main way I think you will see
that you are making progress

00:01:19.280 --> 00:01:25.740
is by having enough input. If you can every day, then do it every day, half an hour or an hour.

00:01:25.740 --> 00:01:31.140
And that will be enough for you to
realize that you are improving each week.

00:01:31.140 --> 00:01:35.000
Another way you can tell that you are getting better

00:01:35.000 --> 00:01:38.800
is by watching a video you saw a long time ago,

00:01:38.800 --> 00:01:43.900
or a video that was still too difficult for you,

00:01:43.900 --> 00:01:47.360
or a video that, well, you understood more or less,

00:01:47.360 --> 00:01:53.320
but if you watch it again after a few
months, or a month or two,

00:01:53.320 --> 00:01:56.740
you will surely realize that
now you understand a lot more,

00:01:56.740 --> 00:01:58.400
that now you understand it much better.

00:01:58.400 --> 00:02:03.740
And I think that that can help you
realize that you are improving, right?

00:02:03.740 --> 00:02:07.840
And as for knowing what level you are at, to know your level,

00:02:07.840 --> 00:02:13.100
it’s as easy as watching Dreaming Spanish videos at different levels,

00:02:13.100 --> 00:02:17.720
or watching or listening to some other podcast for learners of Spanish,

00:02:17.720 --> 00:02:21.540
or *watching various cartoon shows

00:02:21.540 --> 00:02:26.400
or Spanish or Latin American TV series.

00:02:26.400 --> 00:02:31.820
About daily life topics. And if you
can understand it, if you understand all this,

00:02:31.820 --> 00:02:35.340
Well, try to watch TV shows that are a little more difficult,

00:02:35.340 --> 00:02:40.560
shows about police, crime, science fiction, things like that

00:02:40.560 --> 00:02:43.600
that are usually a little harder to understand.

00:02:43.600 --> 00:02:48.000
And then you will realize: "Oh! Look, I can 
understand this. I still can't understand this.

00:02:48.000 --> 00:02:50.800
I still have to improve a little more"', right?

00:02:50.800 --> 00:02:56.780
Another complaint or comment that
I have seen quite a lot in many places is:

00:02:56.780 --> 00:03:01.400
"Ah! But I am not an aural person.

00:03:01.400 --> 00:03:05.740
I am a visual person, or I am a textual person,

00:03:05.740 --> 00:03:10.380
or touch, or nasal", whatever.

00:03:10.380 --> 00:03:14.860
And that, my only answer is no, that does not exist.

00:03:14.860 --> 00:03:19.180
That the Learning Styles hypothesis

00:03:19.180 --> 00:03:22.540
hasn't really been proven. It's not based on anything.

00:03:22.540 --> 00:03:26.680
And that the way a skill is best learned

00:03:26.680 --> 00:03:28.600
depends on the skill itself.

00:03:28.600 --> 00:03:33.240
We can't learn to play tennis or to drive a car by reading a book,

00:03:33.240 --> 00:03:35.220
or by listening to something.

00:03:35.220 --> 00:03:40.500
We cannot learn to play music, to play an instrument by smelling. No.

00:03:40.500 --> 00:03:43.880
For each skill there is a best way to learn it.

00:03:43.880 --> 00:03:47.340
Different people have different interests

00:03:47.340 --> 00:03:50.580
and things they want to do, things they are interested in.

00:03:50.580 --> 00:03:56.460
Some people are more interested in
watching a TV show, watching something fun.

00:03:56.460 --> 00:04:02.200
Other people are more interested in talking with people. In interacting with people.

00:04:02.200 --> 00:04:04.920
And yes. If you are doing an activity

00:04:04.920 --> 00:04:08.180
to which you pay more attention, that interests you more,

00:04:08.180 --> 00:04:11.740
you will remember more things. But that doesn't mean

00:04:11.740 --> 00:04:16.880
that you can learn a language visually or using touch,

00:04:16.880 --> 00:04:20.020
because a language is mainly something spoken.

00:04:20.020 --> 00:04:23.380
Everyone who wants to learn a language and wants to learn to speak,

00:04:23.380 --> 00:04:24.720
has to listen.

00:04:24.720 --> 00:04:28.400
So, I would like us to get rid of this myth

00:04:28.400 --> 00:04:34.040
that each person has to learn things in a different way, right?

00:04:34.040 --> 00:04:37.160
Another question: "Do I need to practice speaking?",

00:04:37.160 --> 00:04:42.260
or "what can I do to practice speaking?" So,

00:04:42.260 --> 00:04:46.160
in general, if you are asking me this question, probably no,

00:04:46.160 --> 00:04:50.440
you don't need to practice talking.
You still don't need to practice speaking.

00:04:50.440 --> 00:04:56.380
I have made an entire video in this course
about how and when to start talking.

00:04:56.380 --> 00:05:01.560
So, if you want more information,
I recommend you watch that video.

00:05:01.560 --> 00:05:08.160
In general, speaking is better later, once you've listened to the language

00:05:08.160 --> 00:05:12.120
for hundreds of hours. At least a few hundred hours

00:05:12.120 --> 00:05:17.220
and you already have a good command
over the grammar, especially basic grammar,

00:05:17.220 --> 00:05:19.340
and enough vocabulary.

00:05:19.340 --> 00:05:25.100
That helps you to continue having
a good accent, good pronunciation,

00:05:25.100 --> 00:05:31.520
and not misusing too much vocabulary and grammar.

00:05:31.520 --> 00:05:38.540
In having a more native-like intuition,
more like that of native speakers of the language, right?

00:05:38.540 --> 00:05:45.940
"Should I practice reading?"
Practicing reading too, like before,

00:05:45.940 --> 00:05:48.700
if you are thinking about practicing reading

00:05:48.700 --> 00:05:52.820
then maybe yes and maybe no.
It depends on what your level is.

00:05:52.820 --> 00:05:57.120
It depends on how many hours of Spanish you've listened to, right?

00:05:57.120 --> 00:06:02.220
And this depends a bit more on you,
if you want to learn Spanish only

00:06:02.220 --> 00:06:06.320
to read or to watch movies or watch TV shows,

00:06:06.320 --> 00:06:10.420
or if you really want to learn to speak

00:06:10.420 --> 00:06:15.520
and to make it easy for other people to understand you.

00:06:15.520 --> 00:06:21.060
And if you want that, it's better to wait a bit to start reading.

00:06:21.060 --> 00:06:26.240
And I made a video. I have made a video about when and how to start reading,

00:06:26.240 --> 00:06:29.680
also in this course,
and I recommend that you watch that video.

00:06:29.680 --> 00:06:33.580
"Should I practice writing?" Writing...

00:06:33.580 --> 00:06:39.720
I'm not sure if later, once you've started reading

00:06:39.720 --> 00:06:46.140
and you have read a lot,
even then I'm still not sure if *writing

00:06:46.140 --> 00:06:50.740
It's something that really helps,
or if it helps much.

00:06:50.740 --> 00:06:54.440
This is something I want to read about.
I want to research a little more.

00:06:54.440 --> 00:06:58.200
I want to read research papers, scientific papers.

00:06:58.200 --> 00:07:03.480
In any case it's not necessary.
It's for sure not necessary because I

00:07:03.480 --> 00:07:06.180
I can write in English

00:07:06.180 --> 00:07:10.220
although in my life I have practiced
very little writing in English.

00:07:10.220 --> 00:07:15.000
Just because I read a lot
I was able to write in English, and write in English,

00:07:15.000 --> 00:07:17.620
well, well, without much trouble.

00:07:17.620 --> 00:07:22.840
Writing might have some benefits,
especially if you want

00:07:22.840 --> 00:07:28.920
Be able to write beautiful Spanish,
artistic Spanish, a novel or a poem and such.

00:07:28.920 --> 00:07:31.940
Some practice may help,

00:07:31.940 --> 00:07:37.220
especially to learn how to order, how to structure text, right?

00:07:37.220 --> 00:07:41.400
But as for Spanish, whether it’s going to help you learn Spanish,

00:07:41.400 --> 00:07:46.100
Right now my belief is that no,
it probably won't help you.

00:07:46.100 --> 00:07:48.900
Another comment or complaint is:

00:07:48.900 --> 00:07:52.600
"Pablo, Pablo, there you made a mistake",
or "there you said something wrong,

00:07:52.600 --> 00:07:54.860
You misused something", right?

00:07:54.860 --> 00:07:58.260
Yes. In my videos I don't have a script.

00:07:58.260 --> 00:08:04.420
Sometimes I have a list of things that
I want to say, that I want to make sure I say,

00:08:04.420 --> 00:08:08.660
But I don't write everything. I do not write Word. By. Word

00:08:08.660 --> 00:08:10.860
everything I'm going to say.

00:08:10.860 --> 00:08:14.620
So, since I am speaking like this, spontaneously,

00:08:14.620 --> 00:08:16.100
I might make a mistake.

00:08:16.100 --> 00:08:18.900
When I talk with my friends,
when I talk with my family,

00:08:18.900 --> 00:08:21.800
well, sometimes I make mistakes too.

00:08:21.800 --> 00:08:26.040
But when children, when babies learn their language,

00:08:26.040 --> 00:08:28.380
learn their mother tongue,

00:08:28.380 --> 00:08:33.680
the people around them,
their family, also make mistakes

00:08:33.680 --> 00:08:37.920
and the children don't learn badly.
The children learn as well

00:08:37.920 --> 00:08:41.360
as the other native speakers around them.

00:08:41.360 --> 00:08:47.480
Just because their parents make
a mistake, make a mistake once,

00:08:47.480 --> 00:08:51.920
It does not mean that the children will learn that mistake because they said it once.

00:08:51.920 --> 00:08:54.740
So, that's why I also recommend

00:08:54.740 --> 00:08:58.320
not watching my videos many times in a row.

00:08:58.320 --> 00:09:02.800
Don't focus on the grammar
or on a certain word that I've used,

00:09:02.800 --> 00:09:07.620
because it might be a mistake. And maybe you start studying it:

00:09:07.620 --> 00:09:11.700
"boli, boli, boli, boli",
you start repeating it in your head,

00:09:11.700 --> 00:09:14.280
or if you start analyzing the grammar,

00:09:14.280 --> 00:09:18.520
you could learn something that is not correct, right?

00:09:18.520 --> 00:09:21.400
That's why I recommend that, instead of doing that,

00:09:21.400 --> 00:09:24.780
to listen a lot, to listen to many different videos.

00:09:24.780 --> 00:09:31.020
And, of course, most of the time
I am not mistaken, I am not making mistakes.

00:09:31.020 --> 00:09:35.160
And if you learn this way you will learn well,
you will not learn my mistakes.

00:09:35.160 --> 00:09:38.180
Another question is:
"Why, Pablo? Why did you say that?

00:09:38.180 --> 00:09:43.320
Why did you use the subjunctive there?
Why did you use 'se'?
But why?
'Se' there doesn't..."

00:09:43.320 --> 00:09:49.560
Let's see, I also explain this in the "Comprehensible Input" video.

00:09:49.560 --> 00:09:53.220
You can watch that video also in this course.

00:09:53.220 --> 00:09:59.740
Languages ​​don't have a reason. Languages, throughout history, evolve,

00:09:59.740 --> 00:10:05.920
and, as language speakers
use it and have different needs,

00:10:05.920 --> 00:10:07.680
The language keeps changing.

00:10:07.680 --> 00:10:12.140
And Spanish now is simply the way Spanish has evolved

00:10:12.140 --> 00:10:15.340
during that time. There is no "why".

00:10:15.340 --> 00:10:19.540
And you don't need to know why, or know a rule,

00:10:19.540 --> 00:10:21.680
to know how to use Spanish.

00:10:21.680 --> 00:10:27.400
The idea of ​​this channel,
the idea of ​​this method, is that you can

00:10:27.400 --> 00:10:32.560
acquire those rules subconsciously, intuitively.

00:10:32.560 --> 00:10:35.680
Simply by encountering them many times.

00:10:35.680 --> 00:10:39.220
The same way children learn, how babies learn.

00:10:39.220 --> 00:10:42.840
They get used to the grammar,
they wouldn't know how to explain it.

00:10:42.840 --> 00:10:47.300
They wouldn't be able to tell you what's a verb, but they can already use the subjunctive, right?

00:10:47.300 --> 00:10:50.580
So, to this question and also to questions like:

00:10:50.580 --> 00:10:54.100
"Oh, make a video to explain

00:10:54.100 --> 00:10:59.140
'se', or to explain the subjunctive, or to explain the past."

00:10:59.140 --> 00:11:03.080
No, I will not do that because
I think it is not useful. What you need

00:11:03.080 --> 00:11:07.460
are videos that you find interesting,
that make you focus

00:11:07.460 --> 00:11:09.960
on the topic,
on the subject being talked about,

00:11:09.960 --> 00:11:14.740
and not in the form of the language,
not in the structure or in certain words.

00:11:14.740 --> 00:11:18.760
Then, another question is: "I'm afraid

00:11:18.760 --> 00:11:22.520
that if I don't know the translation of a word,

00:11:22.520 --> 00:11:28.120
that if I don’t know a grammar rule,
the reason why something is the way it is,

00:11:28.120 --> 00:11:32.140
I'm afraid guessing things wrongly,

00:11:32.140 --> 00:11:36.980
of making up a rule that is not true and learn wrong things. "

00:11:36.980 --> 00:11:41.300
So, you don't have to be afraid of that
because you don't have to guess,

00:11:41.300 --> 00:11:46.100
don't guess, try not to think things like:
"Oh! Why did he say that?

00:11:46.100 --> 00:11:51.900
Maybe here he used the past tense
because he first said this". No.

00:11:51.900 --> 00:11:55.620
Learning with "Comprehensible Input" doesn't mean

00:11:55.620 --> 00:12:00.240
making up the rules,
it doesn't mean guessing the rules

00:12:00.240 --> 00:12:02.780
from the input.

00:12:02.780 --> 00:12:07.080
It means that your brain is going to assimilate everything,

00:12:07.080 --> 00:12:15.540
It will subconsciously deduce everything,
and you don't need to worry. You do not need to think.

00:12:15.540 --> 00:12:19.720
You do not need to guess anything.
You will just get used to it.

00:12:19.720 --> 00:12:22.640
So there is nothing to guess. There is nothing

00:12:22.640 --> 00:12:26.020
to guess wrongly.

00:12:26.020 --> 00:12:30.760
There are also people who ask me what is the difference between two certain words.

00:12:30.760 --> 00:12:33.720
Two words, that either have a similar meaning,

00:12:33.720 --> 00:12:36.940
or that are written or sound similar.

00:12:36.940 --> 00:12:42.140
Please don't do that. There is no need, no reason

00:12:42.140 --> 00:12:43.980
to connect two words

00:12:43.980 --> 00:12:47.420
in your mind just because
the meaning is similar

00:12:47.420 --> 00:12:50.060
or because they are written in a similar way.

00:12:50.060 --> 00:12:53.560
Those words are going to be used differently,

00:12:53.560 --> 00:12:57.180
they will be used in different sentences,
in different contexts,

00:12:57.180 --> 00:13:00.220
in different videos or stories,

00:13:00.220 --> 00:13:05.180
And that is the way to learn them.
The way to learn them is to connect

00:13:05.180 --> 00:13:09.460
every word in your head to the situations in which it appears.

00:13:09.460 --> 00:13:12.680
To the sentences, the other sentences in which it appears.

00:13:12.680 --> 00:13:15.240
And for this other word, to do the same.

00:13:15.240 --> 00:13:18.840
There is never a need to connect
one word to the other one,

00:13:18.840 --> 00:13:22.860
and if you try to do that,
if you try to think of the two words,

00:13:22.860 --> 00:13:26.040
to relate them and to
look at the differences and such,

00:13:26.040 --> 00:13:29.940
what you are going to do is to create
connections between those two words,

00:13:29.940 --> 00:13:33.020
and these connections are going result in that later

00:13:33.020 --> 00:13:37.220
when trying to understand them, or when trying to use them, you will make mistakes.

00:13:37.220 --> 00:13:41.600
You will use the wrong one.
Or every time you need to use that word

00:13:41.600 --> 00:13:46.840
you will have to think: "Which one was it? Was it this one or the other one? Let's see, when...

00:13:46.840 --> 00:13:50.160
when it's a child I have to use this one", right?

00:13:50.160 --> 00:13:52.940
You are going to have to stop and think every time.

00:13:52.940 --> 00:13:57.200
While there was no need to connect these two words.

00:13:57.200 --> 00:14:01.480
These words, if they are each connected to their meaning,

00:14:01.480 --> 00:14:05.280
to their context, you will be able
to use them like a native speaker.

00:14:05.280 --> 00:14:07.220
Another question that I see a lot,

00:14:07.220 --> 00:14:10.720
not asked to me, but that I see it a lot on the internet, is:

00:14:10.720 --> 00:14:14.220
"How do you say this in Spanish?"

00:14:14.220 --> 00:14:18.480
And I think this is the wrong question.
When we learn a language

00:14:18.480 --> 00:14:23.240
we don't learn to say something
that we can say in English, for example.

00:14:23.240 --> 00:14:26.800
We don't learn to translate that think.
But rather, we learn

00:14:26.800 --> 00:14:31.880
something completely different.
It's a different part of our head.

00:14:31.880 --> 00:14:34.260
Other neurons

00:14:34.260 --> 00:14:38.140
where the Spanish expressions and words are built.

00:14:38.140 --> 00:14:41.300
And when we are thinking about a certain thing

00:14:41.300 --> 00:14:45.440
and our level of Spanish is good,
we will know how to say it in Spanish.

00:14:45.440 --> 00:14:48.240
The problem of starting from
a sentence in another language,

00:14:48.240 --> 00:14:51.860
from a sentence in English,
and then trying to translate it,

00:14:51.860 --> 00:14:54.760
is that many times you can't.

00:14:54.760 --> 00:14:58.160
Many times the concept is not even going to be the same,

00:14:58.160 --> 00:15:00.260
because Spanish speakers

00:15:00.260 --> 00:15:03.640
we don't express that concept. We don't express it that way.

00:15:03.640 --> 00:15:07.540
So, the best way to learn to speak Spanish well

00:15:07.540 --> 00:15:11.720
is simply to accept what you learn about Spanish

00:15:11.720 --> 00:15:13.960
is the way things are said,

00:15:13.960 --> 00:15:17.020
and to learn to just go from meaning

00:15:17.020 --> 00:15:20.540
from thought in your head, to Spanish.

00:15:20.540 --> 00:15:25.420
based on all the input you have received,
all your experience with the language.

00:15:25.420 --> 00:15:27.240
Another question is:

00:15:27.240 --> 00:15:32.080
"Pablo, you put a lot of emphasis
on pronunciation, on accent,

00:15:32.080 --> 00:15:35.640
but I don't care about being mistaken for a native speaker.

00:15:35.640 --> 00:15:38.460
I don't care if people know I'm a foreigner.

00:15:38.460 --> 00:15:40.920
Why is it important?

00:15:40.920 --> 00:15:44.680
Well, the reason why

00:15:44.680 --> 00:15:49.400
I recommend that you use a method
that teaches you good pronunciation

00:15:49.400 --> 00:15:53.460
is not to be mistaken for a native speaker.

00:15:53.460 --> 00:15:59.520
I don't even claim that if you follow this
method you will be mistaken for a native speaker,

00:15:59.520 --> 00:16:02.940
because well, there is a lot of variation between people

00:16:02.940 --> 00:16:09.620
and in the end, getting to be mistaken for one is always very difficult.

00:16:09.620 --> 00:16:15.320
But following this method you will
end up with a *very better pronunciation.

00:16:15.320 --> 00:16:17.800
With a much better pronunciation.

00:16:17.800 --> 00:16:21.320
Why is it important?
Because it helps communication.

00:16:21.320 --> 00:16:24.320
The native speakers of that language

00:16:24.320 --> 00:16:29.180
use certain sounds,
certain sounds for the letters,

00:16:29.180 --> 00:16:33.260
certain rhythm, certain intonation of the sentences,

00:16:33.260 --> 00:16:37.680
certain ways to go from one sound to another, right?

00:16:37.680 --> 00:16:41.080
If you don't do it that way, you will have problems.

00:16:41.080 --> 00:16:44.640
If your accent or pronunciation is very bad,

00:16:44.640 --> 00:16:46.920
you'll have a hard time being understood.

00:16:46.920 --> 00:16:50.920
If it is bad but not too bad, then many times

00:16:50.920 --> 00:16:53.720
you will understand each other.
You'll manage to be understood.

00:16:53.720 --> 00:16:59.260
But people are going to have to make a lot of effort, they are going to have to exert themselves,

00:16:59.260 --> 00:17:03.320
to think hard to try to understand what you are saying.

00:17:03.320 --> 00:17:06.520
And that's not ideal. The ideal thing is to have

00:17:06.520 --> 00:17:10.660
a similar pronunciation, very similar to that of native speakers,

00:17:10.660 --> 00:17:13.960
to make it easier for you. To be understood more easily,

00:17:13.960 --> 00:17:16.860
to make it easier to have a conversation

00:17:16.860 --> 00:17:20.300
so people don't get tired when they are talking to you.

00:17:20.300 --> 00:17:24.840
Another question I also see a lot is:
"Which accent is better?"

00:17:24.840 --> 00:17:32.920
There aren't many differences in the Spanish dialects,
in the way they are pronounced,

00:17:32.920 --> 00:17:37.260
There are fewer differences for example
than between British English

00:17:37.260 --> 00:17:41.140
and American English.
Because in British and American English

00:17:41.140 --> 00:17:45.180
change quite a few vowels.
The way many vowels are pronounced changes,

00:17:45.180 --> 00:17:47.720
and that makes it harder to understand.

00:17:47.720 --> 00:17:51.420
In Spanish there are fewer sounds that change.

00:17:51.420 --> 00:17:55.360
There is, depending on the accent, there is only one consonant,

00:17:55.360 --> 00:17:59.080
or two or three consonants that change a bit.

00:17:59.080 --> 00:18:04.120
But in practice it's not going to be
a big impediment for communication.

00:18:04.120 --> 00:18:08.720
And whether you learn a
Latin American or Spanish accent,

00:18:08.720 --> 00:18:10.700
I think you will find it useful

00:18:10.700 --> 00:18:14.480
no matter if you go to Spain or to Latin America.

00:18:14.480 --> 00:18:20.160
There is different vocabulary,
especially colloquial vocabulary.

00:18:20.160 --> 00:18:24.560
Daily life things.
And especially slang.

00:18:24.560 --> 00:18:28.800
And there are differences in vocabulary, for example, for fruits and vegetables

00:18:28.800 --> 00:18:30.860
it's true that there are quite a few differences.

00:18:30.860 --> 00:18:35.600
So, if you already know that
you want to live in a specific country,

00:18:35.600 --> 00:18:39.580
or you are interested in music or literature

00:18:39.580 --> 00:18:41.840
or TV from a specific country,

00:18:41.840 --> 00:18:48.160
then yes, try to have more input, try to listen to
and read more things from that country, right?

00:18:48.160 --> 00:18:53.800
And if you want to speak with
the accent of a specific country,

00:18:53.800 --> 00:19:01.160
it's also a good idea to listen
mainly to people from that country.

00:19:01.160 --> 00:19:05.240
But that's a bit more of a personal preference.

00:19:05.240 --> 00:19:11.700
And if you want to learn
Spanish from El Salvador

00:19:11.700 --> 00:19:16.140
and you don't find much content,
enough videos or radio from El Salvador,

00:19:16.140 --> 00:19:21.340
Well look, maybe you are going to have to
learn Spanish, I don't know, from Mexico or Colombia.

00:19:21.340 --> 00:19:24.740
Maybe similar to El Salvador's, but not exactly the same.

00:19:24.740 --> 00:19:29.400
At least until you later have the opportunity of going to live in El Salvador.

00:19:29.400 --> 00:19:34.180
And maybe there you then can learn more about the vocabulary

00:19:34.180 --> 00:19:35.840
and the pronunciation of that place, right?

00:19:35.840 --> 00:19:40.460
Finally, the last question is also a bit related.

00:19:40.460 --> 00:19:42.620
The question is:

00:19:42.620 --> 00:19:47.220
"If I want to speak with a Latin American accent
or I want to speak with a Spanish accent,

00:19:47.220 --> 00:19:53.000
Do you think it's bad to hear Spanish from another place,
Spanish from another country?

00:19:53.000 --> 00:19:55.820
If I want to speak with a Spanish accent from Spain,

00:19:55.820 --> 00:19:59.300
Is it bad to listen to Spanish from Latin America?"

00:19:59.300 --> 00:20:05.520
It depends. It depends.
In the end, the way we speak

00:20:05.520 --> 00:20:08.800
depends a lot on what we identify with.

00:20:08.800 --> 00:20:14.540
If the people who are our friends,
who are our family, who are our idols,

00:20:14.540 --> 00:20:20.540
speak in a certain way, we will probably end up speaking like them.

00:20:20.540 --> 00:20:22.700
If you live in Spain

00:20:22.700 --> 00:20:28.020
and you have friends in Spain,
you will probably end up speaking a lot like them, right?

00:20:28.020 --> 00:20:32.920
But of course, if most of your input,
what you hear, what you read

00:20:32.920 --> 00:20:36.640
before going to Spain is from Latin America,

00:20:36.640 --> 00:20:39.820
Well, you are going to learn Spanish
from Latin America, of course.

00:20:39.820 --> 00:20:42.240
And the opposite case.
If you go Latin America

00:20:42.240 --> 00:20:45.740
but you listen mainly to my videos or other Spaniards,

00:20:45.740 --> 00:20:51.480
Well, you are going to speak mostly
with vocabulary and pronunciation from Spain.

00:20:51.480 --> 00:20:55.800
There are many people who after they
move to a Latin American country

00:20:55.800 --> 00:20:58.960
will very soon start talking like the people there,

00:20:58.960 --> 00:21:03.180
with the vocabulary and the accent of the locals.

00:21:03.180 --> 00:21:06.420
But it's different for every person

00:21:06.420 --> 00:21:11.680
There are people who identify a lot
with their own identity, right?

00:21:11.680 --> 00:21:15.420
And even if they live in a foreign country, they don't change, or barely change

00:21:15.420 --> 00:21:17.980
the way they talk.

00:21:17.980 --> 00:21:22.440
But hey, it's up to you, To how important it is for you

00:21:22.440 --> 00:21:27.360
to speak with the accent or dialect of a particular country.

00:21:27.360 --> 00:21:31.880
And if you want to speak with that country's (dialect),
then yes, I recommend that a large part

00:21:31.880 --> 00:21:34.980
of the input you receive,
of the Spanish you hear,

00:21:34.980 --> 00:21:36.680
be from that place, right?

00:21:36.680 --> 00:21:41.880
And that's it, this is the end of
the questions and answers videos.

00:21:41.880 --> 00:21:46.980
I hope you found this information helpful.
Okay?

00:21:46.980 --> 00:21:49.380
Alright, see you later!

title: How to Learn a Language #2: What Is Comprehensible Input?
description: This fundamental concept from linguistics research explains how we actually acquire languages. It is the foundation upon which the Dreaming Spanish method is built upon. We explain more in this video.
subtitles:
WEBVTT
Kind: captions
Language: en

00:00:00.540 --> 00:00:02.460
Hi! What's up?

00:00:02.460 --> 00:00:06.840
Today I'm going to explain what Comprehensible Input is.

00:00:07.100 --> 00:00:14.200
I am going to explain why it is the way we really acquire a language,

00:00:14.200 --> 00:00:17.680
the way how can we really manage

00:00:17.680 --> 00:00:24.680
to speak a language fluently and why is the only way that really results

00:00:24.720 --> 00:00:32.040
in the same kind of language knowledge that native speakers have.

00:00:32.080 --> 00:00:35.440
So, where does Comprehensible Input come from?

00:00:35.560 --> 00:00:41.280
Comprehensible Input has been something that has existed in the research

00:00:41.360 --> 00:00:45.460
about language acquisition, about language learning,

00:00:45.460 --> 00:00:50.720
since the 70s. It has been researched since the 70s.

00:00:50.720 --> 00:00:53.800
Before that, there were already researchers

00:00:53.820 --> 00:00:58.920
that pointed in this direction, but since the 70s,

00:00:58.920 --> 00:01:01.200
and especially with Stephen Krashen,

00:01:01.200 --> 00:01:06.700
It has become better understood and has been studied more in detail.

00:01:06.720 --> 00:01:13.580
So, what is the main idea of ​​Comprehensible Input"?

00:01:13.580 --> 00:01:18.560
The idea is that for our brain

00:01:18.560 --> 00:01:23.580
to learn a language, learn words, learn the grammar,

00:01:23.580 --> 00:01:29.880
we need to receive input,

00:01:29.880 --> 00:01:33.240
either listening or reading,

00:01:33.240 --> 00:01:35.900
and we have to understand that input.

00:01:35.900 --> 00:01:38.400
We have to know what it says here.

00:01:38.400 --> 00:01:42.180
Or we have to know what that person is saying.

00:01:42.180 --> 00:01:47.400
Our brain really has to directly connect the meaning

00:01:47.400 --> 00:01:51.900
with the words, with the words we are hearing.

00:01:51.900 --> 00:01:58.580
And Comprehensible Input also says that that's the only think that's needed,

00:01:58.580 --> 00:02:03.360
that that is the only thing that's necessary.

00:02:03.360 --> 00:02:07.560
Yes, only input, and input that we understand.

00:02:07.560 --> 00:02:10.840
And well, it's the only necessary thing,

00:02:10.840 --> 00:02:12.960
but it's also implied

00:02:12.960 --> 00:02:17.900
that to be listening or reading and understand things

00:02:17.900 --> 00:02:21.460
we also need to be paying attention, right?

00:02:21.460 --> 00:02:25.420
We have to be interested in what's going on

00:02:25.420 --> 00:02:27.800
to really be listening.

00:02:27.800 --> 00:02:30.540
And we also need to be interested

00:02:30.540 --> 00:02:33.780
in order to remember more things,

00:02:33.780 --> 00:02:39.340
so that our memory really stores the things that are happening, right?

00:02:39.340 --> 00:02:42.340
And the idea of ​​Comprehensible Input, is also

00:02:42.340 --> 00:02:46.380
is that if we are taught grammar rules,

00:02:46.380 --> 00:02:48.680
we are taught how to conjugate a verb

00:02:48.680 --> 00:02:52.420
or we are taught word order, if we get explanations

00:02:52.420 --> 00:02:54.440
or learn the rules

00:02:54.440 --> 00:02:57.620
then ok, maybe rationally

00:02:57.620 --> 00:03:02.040
we know the rule. We consciously know the rule.

00:03:02.040 --> 00:03:05.720
But that doesn't mean we know how to speak.

00:03:05.720 --> 00:03:11.100
It does not mean that we can apply that rule when speaking.

00:03:11.100 --> 00:03:15.620
It makes a distinction between conscious knowledge

00:03:15.620 --> 00:03:19.400
and unconscious or intuitive knowledge.

00:03:19.400 --> 00:03:23.380
And Comprehensible Input says we need to build this type

00:03:23.380 --> 00:03:25.700
of intuitive knowledge.

00:03:25.700 --> 00:03:31.420
Because with explicit knowledge, with knowledge of the rules,

00:03:31.420 --> 00:03:38.280
well, it can be useful if for example we are writing, we have time to think,

00:03:38.280 --> 00:03:42.600
and we remember dozens and dozens of rules,

00:03:42.600 --> 00:03:47.140
it may help us form a sentence

00:03:47.140 --> 00:03:49.860
that we couldn't form otherwise, right?

00:03:49.860 --> 00:03:52.600
But in the end it's like a trap, it's

00:03:52.600 --> 00:03:56.920
something we can do because we have time.

00:03:56.920 --> 00:04:01.400
because, well, yes, maybe we remember the rules

00:04:01.400 --> 00:04:04.960
but it's not very useful in real life.

00:04:04.960 --> 00:04:09.400
If we are talking to a person, or if we have to write something

00:04:09.400 --> 00:04:14.580
and we have to write a lot of text, we can't really spend time thinking every single sentence,

00:04:14.580 --> 00:04:17.300
applying dozens and dozens of rules.

00:04:17.300 --> 00:04:21.660
So, that is basically Comprehensible Input.

00:04:21.660 --> 00:04:27.480
What's the matter? That in the 70s, when Comprehensible Input appeared,

00:04:27.720 --> 00:04:33.880
the majority of researchers, the majority of scientists researching language learning

00:04:33.880 --> 00:04:36.820
disagreed with it because it was something new,

00:04:36.820 --> 00:04:41.660
it wasn't what they had been working on for so many years, right?

00:04:41.660 --> 00:04:45.100
So, at the beginning many researchers

00:04:45.100 --> 00:04:48.580
didn't accept that Comprehensible Input

00:04:48.580 --> 00:04:52.360
was necessary. They thought it was not necessary.

00:04:52.360 --> 00:04:57.220
What then? With years and years of research and more and more papers,

00:04:57.220 --> 00:05:01.460
more and more researchers began to accept

00:05:01.460 --> 00:05:06.220
that ok, maybe yes. Maybe Comprehensible Input is necessary,

00:05:06.220 --> 00:05:10.380
because it is true that in all situations where people manage

00:05:10.380 --> 00:05:13.200
to learn a language to fluency

00:05:13.200 --> 00:05:17.660
it is true that they were receiving some kind of comprehensible input, right?

00:05:17.660 --> 00:05:21.520
They agreed that it is necessary, but

00:05:21.520 --> 00:05:23.880
they didn't think it is sufficient.

00:05:23.880 --> 00:05:28.600
They believed that only comprehensible input is not enough

00:05:28.600 --> 00:05:32.080
that something else was needed, you had to have something else.

00:05:32.080 --> 00:05:36.100
What happened then? That with more and more years of research

00:05:36.100 --> 00:05:41.500
it became apparent that comprehensible input was sufficient,

00:05:41.510 --> 00:05:43.820
that with only comprehensible input

00:05:43.820 --> 00:05:48.740
we can get to speak a language and speak it well and fluently.

00:05:48.740 --> 00:05:51.540
What happened next? That these researchers

00:05:51.540 --> 00:05:55.360
then said: "Ok, ok, it IS enough,

00:05:55.360 --> 00:05:59.340
but it's not the best, it's not the best way, it's not the fastest".

00:05:59.340 --> 00:06:03.080
"There are other ways, or other things you can do

00:06:03.080 --> 00:06:09.060
together with comprehensible input, to learn better to learn faster".

00:06:09.060 --> 00:06:13.060
But the issue is that right now we have a lot of data

00:06:13.060 --> 00:06:16.600
that show that comprehensible input

00:06:16.600 --> 00:06:20.700
is very good, that you can reach a good level at a language.

00:06:20.700 --> 00:06:24.260
that it's fast. And they're having a hard time proving

00:06:24.260 --> 00:06:30.820
that with explicit knowledge, studying vocabulary, studying grammar

00:06:30.820 --> 00:06:36.280
you can learn better than with comprehensible input. They're having a hard time.

00:06:36.280 --> 00:06:39.340
And I think the next obvious step

00:06:39.340 --> 00:06:45.400
is that they will accept that comprehensible input is the fastest, and the best.

00:06:45.400 --> 00:06:50.360
And the next step will be that they will probably end up accepting

00:06:50.360 --> 00:06:54.780
that studying grammar, studying vocabulary,

00:06:54.780 --> 00:06:59.480
and other types of conscious study, can be bad.

00:06:59.480 --> 00:07:06.500
It can be worse than doing nothing. It can be worse than studying only with comprehensible input

00:07:06.500 --> 00:07:09.960
and that we can end up with worse results

00:07:09.960 --> 00:07:13.740
if we do this kind of study, conscious study, right?

00:07:13.740 --> 00:07:17.380
And probably research will advance in this direction.

00:07:17.380 --> 00:07:21.900
Because right now we have papers, quite a few papers,

00:07:21.900 --> 00:07:25.800
that show that people who have studied in class

00:07:25.800 --> 00:07:30.280
they end up with a worse grammar level, making more mistakes.

00:07:30.280 --> 00:07:34.020
There is also data showing that people trying to practice

00:07:34.020 --> 00:07:37.960
talking, try to practice pronounciation, people who talk a lot,

00:07:37.960 --> 00:07:41.100
end up with worse pronunciation

00:07:41.100 --> 00:07:46.020
than people who wait or people who don't talk so much, who don't produce so much.

00:07:46.020 --> 00:07:51.940
So I just explained to you why I think Comprehensible Input works,

00:07:51.940 --> 00:07:55.920
and that Comprehensible Input is the best way to learn a language.

00:07:55.920 --> 00:08:00.140
But now I want to provide examples, I want

00:08:00.140 --> 00:08:03.500
provide more information so that you understand

00:08:03.500 --> 00:08:09.500
what things are Comprehensible Input and what things are not Comprehensible Input.

00:08:09.500 --> 00:08:13.040
For example, a dad or a mom

00:08:13.040 --> 00:08:15.760
reading a tale to their children.

00:08:15.760 --> 00:08:21.680
When the child is in bed, the dad or mom is reading them a story, right?

00:08:21.680 --> 00:08:24.400
That is comprehensible input.

00:08:24.400 --> 00:08:27.820
The dad or mom is talking to the child

00:08:27.820 --> 00:08:33.460
at a level that the child understands, using words that are not too difficult for the child

00:08:33.460 --> 00:08:36.720
If there are any words in the book that are a bit difficult,

00:08:36.720 --> 00:08:43.240
the dad or the mom can explain it in a different way. They can explain it with easier words.

00:08:43.240 --> 00:08:48.600
And the child's attention is on the story. Their attention

00:08:48.600 --> 00:08:52.360
is not on the words, or on the grammar.

00:08:52.360 --> 00:08:55.520
And this is another important

00:08:55.520 --> 00:09:00.500
about Comprehensible Input.

00:09:00.500 --> 00:09:03.980
Attention needs to be on the meaning.

00:09:03.980 --> 00:09:06.960
We need to be trying to understand

00:09:06.960 --> 00:09:10.140
what's going on. Understand what's being said to us.

00:09:10.140 --> 00:09:14.840
If our mind is thinking about the past, or the subjunctive,

00:09:14.840 --> 00:09:18.100
or in anything about the grammar or the vocabulary,

00:09:18.100 --> 00:09:21.260
We are not paying attention to meaning.

00:09:21.260 --> 00:09:27.220
We are not paying attention to the meaning of what we are reading or what we are being told.

00:09:27.220 --> 00:09:31.880
For example, imagine that you have a tutor, a Spanish tutor,

00:09:31.880 --> 00:09:34.840
that is teaching you Spanish

00:09:34.840 --> 00:09:38.960
And the tutor brings fruit to the class, a lot of different fruits.

00:09:38.960 --> 00:09:43.260
And she grabs a banana and says: "banana".

00:09:43.260 --> 00:09:48.160
Okay. She grabs an apple and says: "apple".

00:09:48.160 --> 00:09:52.300
She grabs an orange and says: "orange."

00:09:52.300 --> 00:09:55.360
Is this comprehensible input?

00:09:55.360 --> 00:10:00.660
Let's see, there is some input. You are listening to words, right?

00:10:00.660 --> 00:10:08.880
Is it comprehensible? Yes. You are understanding that the words are the names of the fruits. Yes, you are understanding it.

00:10:08.880 --> 00:10:15.640
But this is the worst quality of comprehensible input quality you can get.

00:10:15.640 --> 00:10:20.140
It's the lowest quality comprehensible input.

00:10:20.140 --> 00:10:22.680
Because these words

00:10:22.680 --> 00:10:27.580
are not connecting with anything that is important to you,

00:10:27.580 --> 00:10:31.840
Your tutor is not explaining how to make a fruit salad,

00:10:31.840 --> 00:10:37.420
and she is not explaining to you what fruits she likes, what fruits she doesn't like,

00:10:37.420 --> 00:10:40.200
what fruits people eat in their country...

00:10:40.200 --> 00:10:45.520
When words are part of some sort of activity,

00:10:45.520 --> 00:10:49.080
of something that is important to us,

00:10:49.080 --> 00:10:51.740
is when we really remember.

00:10:51.740 --> 00:10:57.600
It's when we can really connect it with other things in our head.

00:10:57.600 --> 00:11:00.940
We can connect it with other words we know,

00:11:00.940 --> 00:11:03.900
we can connect it with a situation

00:11:03.900 --> 00:11:06.520
in which we were talking to a person

00:11:06.520 --> 00:11:09.000
who was was explaining something to us.

00:11:09.000 --> 00:11:10.740
Come on, another example.

00:11:10.740 --> 00:11:15.600
An app on your phone, an application

00:11:15.600 --> 00:11:22.220
that shows you a picture, it shows you a drawing, and you have to remember

00:11:22.220 --> 00:11:30.300
how to say that word in Spanish, or how to say it in the language you are learning.

00:11:30.300 --> 00:11:32.500
Is this comprehensible input?

00:11:32.500 --> 00:11:35.960
No, it's not comprehensible input, because there is no input.

00:11:35.960 --> 00:11:39.500
They are trying to make you produce,

00:11:39.500 --> 00:11:43.320
to make you produce output, right? To get you to speak or to write.

00:11:43.320 --> 00:11:49.300
In this case it is not comprehensible input, and is not useful to learn a language.

00:11:49.300 --> 00:11:55.280
Applications like Duolingo, right? They give you some words, they give you several words

00:11:55.280 --> 00:12:00.180
and you have to place them in order. Is it comprehensible input?

00:12:00.180 --> 00:12:06.980
Well, no, it's not input. They are making you produce. They are making you put together a whole sentence,

00:12:06.980 --> 00:12:12.780
and it's not even good output, because never ever when you're talking to someone

00:12:12.780 --> 00:12:16.760
will they give you a few words and: There you have! Put them together! Right?

00:12:16.760 --> 00:12:19.080
No, that's not how speaking a language works.

00:12:19.080 --> 00:12:23.100
So, I hope that these examples will make it clearer

00:12:23.100 --> 00:12:28.620
what things are Comprehensible Input and what things are not Comprehensible Input.

00:12:28.620 --> 00:12:31.860
A detail that I want to clarify,

00:12:31.860 --> 00:12:34.700
that I want to make sure you know

00:12:34.700 --> 00:12:38.760
is that as I said before, comprehensible input

00:12:38.760 --> 00:12:42.920
is not about using the conscious part of our mind.

00:12:42.920 --> 00:12:47.960
We use the conscious part when somebody explains a grammar rule to us,

00:12:47.960 --> 00:12:53.420
but we also use it when we ourselves think

00:12:53.420 --> 00:12:58.120
in grammar rules, or when we deduce them.

00:12:58.120 --> 00:13:01.540
We are listening to someone speak to us in Spanish

00:13:01.540 --> 00:13:04.660
and we begin to think: "Ah! Well, I think

00:13:04.660 --> 00:13:08.880
that when they say this then they use the subjunctive."

00:13:08.880 --> 00:13:12.800
This is still the conscious part of our brain.

00:13:12.800 --> 00:13:14.960
This is not Comprehensible Input.

00:13:14.960 --> 00:13:18.820
Comprehensible Input does not mean to read or listen

00:13:18.820 --> 00:13:23.220
and to try to think ourselves about grammar rules, no.

00:13:23.220 --> 00:13:28.540
Comprehensible Input uses the subconscious part of the brain.

00:13:28.540 --> 00:13:31.500
It means that listening and understanding

00:13:31.500 --> 00:13:36.380
we will acquire the grammar, we will get used to the grammar

00:13:36.380 --> 00:13:42.120
and we will be able to use it. We do not have to think. No need to think about:

00:13:42.120 --> 00:13:47.720
"Oh! Let's see what the rule is here. Let's see why he used the subjunctive here

00:13:47.720 --> 00:13:50.860
or why he used this past and not the other one." No.

00:13:50.860 --> 00:13:53.200
This is not comprehensible input.

00:13:53.200 --> 00:13:59.480
And well, finally stress, I want to emphasize what I said before

00:13:59.480 --> 00:14:04.760
that comprehensible input, yes, we need input, listening or reading,

00:14:04.760 --> 00:14:09.160
we need it to be comprehensible, that we understand it,

00:14:09.160 --> 00:14:14.360
but it’s also very useful to pay attention,

00:14:14.360 --> 00:14:17.920
to be interested in what is being told to us.

00:14:17.920 --> 00:14:23.080
Therefore, ideally this input should be: either a lot of fun,

00:14:23.080 --> 00:14:27.680
so much fun and so funny that we want to hear more and more;

00:14:27.680 --> 00:14:33.900
something that is important for our life, something that will help us in life;

00:14:33.900 --> 00:14:38.880
or something we are interested in, either some news story or fact

00:14:38.880 --> 00:14:42.220
or we are interested in history, for example,

00:14:42.220 --> 00:14:46.700
We can listen to content or read content

00:14:46.700 --> 00:14:49.680
about history, about some topic that we find interesting.

00:14:49.680 --> 00:14:54.000
And this is the end of the video about comprehensible input.

00:14:54.000 --> 00:14:57.760
In the following videos I will explain

00:14:57.760 --> 00:15:00.780
how to make the most of Dreaming Spanish,

00:15:00.780 --> 00:15:05.380
how to learn using Dreaming Spanish and using other resources too.

00:15:05.380 --> 00:15:09.160
Ok? So, see you in the next video.
